items.title: Yazd Solar Nexus
items.body:
Idea (short):
Turn Yazd into a flagship solar powered city combining large scale solar, water production, and AI driven industry in the desert.
Why Yazd (with numbers):

~300 sunny days/year and ~2,000–2,200 kWh/m²/year solar irradiance
Vast nearby desert land → >10 GW solar potential within ~100 km radius
Close to central grid and cities like Isfahan and Kerman
Existing desert architecture optimized for extreme heat

What it looks like:

5–10 GW solar farms powering homes, industry, and exports
Solar powered desalination + water pipelines enabling green zones
New districts for AI, materials, and advanced manufacturing
Urban design combining badgirs + modern cooling + shaded streets

Why this works:

Solar is among the lowest cost energy sources globally
Desert land has low opportunity cost
Energy can be exported as electricity, hydrogen, or compute
Reduces pressure on water stressed regions

Impact:

Replace part of oil revenue with clean energy exports
Create 100k+ jobs across energy and tech
Scalable model for Kerman, Semnan, and beyond

items.title: Reorganization as a Service for Iran: Building Specialized Transformation Companies, with NPC as a Pilot
items.body:
[author removed]
Process / industrial development background, Master of Chemical Engineering (Sharif University), Master of Project Management, Calgary University, 22 Years of Experience in the oil, gas, and petrochemical sector.
Abstract
Iran will need a new class of reorganization and transformation companies to help large industrial groups become more agile, more transparent, and more profitable. These firms would focus on governance redesign, operating model improvement, capital allocation, project prioritization, treasury discipline, export strategy, and technical standards.
A strong pilot case is the petrochemical sector. Iran’s petrochemical industry already operates 79 production complexes and has surpassed 100 million tons per year of nominal capacity. Official guidance in 2025 projected capacity reaching 105 million tons/year by March 2026, with exports of roughly 34.8 million tons worth about $13.6 billion. This scale is large enough to justify specialized restructuring and performance-improvement firms.
NPC can be used as the model: not as a command-and-control bureaucracy, but as a single commercial and strategic umbrella for petrochemicals, while plant operations remain decentralized.
Why It’s Interesting
This idea matters because post-transition Iran will not only need new projects; it will need better institutions and better company models. Many industrial groups will require restructuring before they can attract investors, lenders, technology partners, and high-quality management teams.
The petrochemical sector is the clearest example because it is already one of the main pillars of Iran’s non-oil economy, yet it still faces bottlenecks in efficiency, value-chain completion, and balanced development.
International governance benchmarks also support this direction. The OECD’s 2024 SOE Guidelines emphasize that the state should act as an active, informed, and professional owner, with competent boards and high standards of transparency, disclosure, and accountability. That is exactly the kind of framework Iran will need in rebuilding large industrial groups.
Approach
The idea is to create specialized Iranian reorganization companies that help large enterprises redesign themselves to improve performance, financial viability, and growth.
Example: NPC (National Petrochemical Co.) as a pilot case
NPC should be rebuilt as the single commercial and strategic umbrella for Iran’s petrochemical sector. This does not mean every plant is run from cpital. It means the following functions are centralized:
•	Export marketing and customer portfolio management
•	International trading and logistics
•	Treasury and FX risk management
•	Project finance interface and lender data room
•	Common HSE, technical, and procurement standards
•	Portfolio capital allocation and value-chain prioritization
At the same time, site operations remain decentralized, with each complex responsible for production, maintenance, reliability, staffing, and day-to-day execution.
Operating principle
The model is simple:
Centralized at the umbrella level	Decentralized at site level
Export marketing	                        Plant operations
Trading and logistics	                 Maintenance and reliability
Treasury / FX risk	                          Local staffing
Financing interface	                          Day-to-day production planning
Technical / HSE standards	          Site execution
Portfolio capital allocation	          Operational improvement
What these new firms would do
A reorganization company in Iran could offer services such as:
•	Corporate restructuring and operating-model redesign
•	Governance and board reform
•	KPI and performance system development
•	Treasury and working-capital discipline
•	CAPEX prioritization and value-chain strategy
•	Investor readiness and lender reporting support
•	Procurement, HSE, and technical standardization
•	Post-merger or post-consolidation integration support
Reorganization should be one of the first priorities in rebuilding Iran’s industrial sector. A strong example is the petrochemical industry, where NPC can be re-established as the single commercial and strategic umbrella for the sector. This does not mean every plant should be controlled from Tehran. Instead, plant operations should remain decentralized, while key functions such as export marketing, international trading, logistics, treasury, foreign exchange risk management, project finance coordination, common HSE and technical standards, procurement standards, and portfolio capital allocation are centralized under one professional structure.
This model would reduce duplication, eliminate unnecessary parallel offices, strengthen Iran’s petrochemical brand in international markets, improve credibility with investors and lenders, and help direct capital toward higher-value opportunities across the value chain. It would also create demand for a new generation of Iranian reorganization and turnaround companies that could help modernize large industrial groups and prepare them for sustainable growth.

items.title: Manufacturing for those who stood by us (Strategic)
items.body:
Core idea

Iran can become a major new manufacturing base during reconstruction and stabilization
The goal should not be cheap labor only
The goal should be a modern, export focused, green industrial platform

Why Iran

Large dry and desert areas are well suited for solar and wind powered industrial zones
Startup costs for factories and industrial infrastructure could be relatively low
Currency exchange can make entry easier for countries like the US and its partners
Iran’s location is strong for logistics and export to Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia, South Asia, and nearby markets

Strategic advantages

Iran has a capable, educated, and technically strong population
Iranian society is generally open to working with Western experts and firms
Foreign engineers and specialists could operate in Iran more easily than in many other regional markets, especially with early safety and housing support

Industrial development model

New foreign manufacturers should be encouraged to use clean energy as much as possible
Domestic Iranian manufacturers should be brought into the supply chain as providers of parts, materials, and services
Investment should help build a wider local industrial ecosystem, not isolated foreign owned plants

Local participation requirements

Foreign companies should be expected to transfer knowledge and train Iranian talent
There should be minimum local workforce participation targets at every level:

executives
directors
managers
engineers
technicians
plant workers


The model should build long term Iranian capability, not just use Iran as a low cost production base

Partnership approach

Countries and institutions that stood with the Iranian people early should be given early access, preferred terms, or targeted incentives
This can help create future strategic bonds based on trust and shared long term interest

Main discussion questions

Which industries should be prioritized first?
Which regions are best for green energy powered industrial zones?
What incentives should be offered to early partner countries and companies?
How should local participation and knowledge transfer requirements be defined and enforced?
How can domestic Iranian suppliers be integrated from the beginning?
What legal, safety, and infrastructure guarantees are needed in the early phase?

Closing thought

Iran should reopen as a green manufacturing and logistics platform that attracts capital, builds Iranian capability, rewards trusted partners, and creates long term strategic alliances

items.title: Cloud Migration and Modernization Studio
items.body:
[author removed]
Cloud / Backend Engineer with experience in AWS, backend systems, API architecture, authentication, and workflow-driven product design.
Abstract
A studio that helps Iranian companies modernize legacy software, infrastructure, and operations by moving from outdated on-premise or fragmented systems to secure, scalable cloud-based platforms.
The studio would begin as a services-led business, helping organizations assess current systems, design migration plans, rebuild critical components, and adopt modern engineering practices. Over time, it would evolve into a productized platform with reusable migration toolkits, architecture templates, security modules, and operational dashboards.
The goal is to reduce the time, risk, and cost of modernization for Iranian businesses entering a more open and competitive economy.
Why It’s Interesting
If Iran becomes open to global markets, many local companies will face immediate pressure to compete with better-equipped foreign firms. Many businesses will still be operating on legacy systems, manual processes, disconnected software, and weak infrastructure.
This creates a major gap:
•	companies need modernization
•	internal teams may not know how to do it
•	foreign vendors may be expensive or poorly localized
•	migration projects are risky without local execution capability
This idea is interesting because it solves a foundational problem rather than a surface problem. Modern software, secure infrastructure, clean APIs, proper authentication, observability, and automation are the base layer for growth across banking, healthcare, logistics, retail, manufacturing, education, and other sectors.
Instead of building one more app, this idea builds the capability that allows many future apps and businesses to exist.
Problem Solved
Many organizations have one or more of these issues:
•	legacy systems that are expensive to maintain
•	business-critical workflows trapped in spreadsheets or manual steps
•	poor system integration across departments
•	weak security and identity management
•	no cloud strategy
•	no observability, automation, or deployment discipline
•	slow delivery of new products and features
Without solving this, many firms will fail to scale, fail to compete, or waste years on bad digital transformation efforts.
This studio would help them modernize in a structured and practical way.
Approach
The project can be developed in three phases.
Phase 1 — Services-led modernization studio
Start with a consulting and delivery model focused on:
•	cloud readiness assessments
•	legacy system audits
•	migration roadmaps
•	API modernization
•	identity and access redesign
•	CI/CD setup
•	monitoring and operational maturity
•	application decomposition into modern services where needed
Target early customers:
•	private healthcare groups
•	financial services firms
•	insurance businesses
•	logistics companies
•	education providers
•	high-growth SMEs
Phase 2 — Productized accelerators
Convert repeated delivery patterns into reusable assets:
•	reference architectures
•	secure IAM/auth starter kits
•	API gateway templates
•	observability dashboards
•	migration checklists and scoring tools
•	data migration frameworks
•	environment provisioning blueprints
•	compliance and audit logging modules
This reduces delivery cost and increases consistency.
Phase 3 — Platform layer
Build a software platform around the studio’s delivery model:
•	modernization assessment portal
•	migration planning dashboard
•	system inventory and dependency mapping
•	rollout tracking
•	risk scoring
•	cost estimation
•	architecture recommendation engine
•	post-migration health dashboards
At this stage, the business shifts from pure services to a mix of services and recurring software revenue.
Example Use Cases
•	A clinic group moving from local servers and spreadsheets to a cloud-based operating platform
•	A logistics company replacing disconnected systems with integrated APIs and dashboards
•	An insurance firm modernizing authentication, reporting, and customer workflows
•	A growing enterprise setting up secure cloud landing zones, deployment pipelines, and access controls
•	A company preparing to integrate with foreign partners, vendors, or SaaS tools
Why Iran
A newly open Iran would likely face a wave of digital catch-up across both private and public-facing sectors. Many businesses would need modernization before they could truly absorb foreign investment, compete regionally, or operate efficiently.
Iran would not only need new startups. It would need serious modernization of existing institutions and businesses. This project addresses that gap.
Expected Impact
•	faster digital transformation for local companies
•	lower modernization risk
•	improved business productivity
•	better security and operational reliability
•	stronger local engineering capability
•	creation of a local modernization ecosystem instead of dependency on foreign consultancies alone
Business Model
Possible revenue streams:
•	assessment and advisory fees
•	fixed-price migration projects
•	architecture and implementation retainers
•	managed platform subscriptions
•	licensing reusable modernization toolkits
•	ongoing support and observability packages
Initial MVP
A realistic MVP is not a full platform. It is a focused studio offering with a few reusable tools:
•	cloud readiness assessment template
•	system modernization scorecard
•	migration roadmap generator
•	reference architecture pack
•	sample observability dashboard
•	sample secure identity/access design
•	one pilot migration case study
This is enough to validate demand and establish credibility.
Help Needed
•	enterprise architects
•	cloud engineers
•	security / IAM specialists
•	DevOps engineers
•	sector advisors from healthcare, finance, logistics, and education
•	design partner companies willing to run pilot modernization projects
•	legal/compliance advisors for regulated industries
•	funding for initial tooling, pilots, and team formation

items.title: فرهنگ سازی هدفمند در ایران پس از جمهوری اسلامی
items.body:
ایران پس از سال ها حکومت پرتناقض جمهوری اسلامی، با مشکلات جدی فرهنگی و تناقض های عجیب در رفتارهای اجتماعی روبه رو شده است.
اگر قرار است ایران به کشوری قوی، امن، جذاب برای زندگی، و مناسب برای جذب سرمایه تبدیل شود، فرهنگ سازی جدی و هدفمند لازم خواهد بود.
یکی از راه های عملی می تواند ایجاد تیم های فرهنگی و هنری برای تولید تیزرهای کوتاه آموزشی و تبلیغاتی برای تلویزیون و رسانه های عمومی باشد. این تیزرها می توانند به شکل روشن، جذاب، و محترمانه، به آموزش رفتار درست اجتماعی کمک کنند و به مرور زمان الگوهای سالم تری را در جامعه جا بیندازند.
برای نمونه، فضاهای اجتماعی جدید یا کمتر تجربه شده مانند نایت کلاب ها، مهمانی ها، تجمع های بزرگ، و فضاهای تفریحی مدرن، نیاز به آموزش مداوم دارند. موضوعاتی مانند رفتار محترمانه، رعایت مرزهای فردی، و جلوگیری از مزاحمت های فرهنگی، مذهبی، اجتماعی، و جنسی باید به شکل روشن و قابل فهم آموزش داده شوند.
هدف این تیزرها نباید تحقیر، توهین، یا نصیحت کردن مردم باشد. هدف باید فقط فرهنگ سازی، آموزش، و نشان دادن الگوهای سالم رفتاری باشد.
ویژگی های این تیزرها

از نظر ساخت، جذاب و حرفه ای باشند
رفتار نادرست و رفتار درست را در کنار هم نشان دهند
کوتاه و قابل فهم باشند
خسته کننده نباشند
بدون توهین و فقط با هدف آموزش و فرهنگ سازی ساخته شوند

نحوه پخش
این ویدئوها باید برای گروه های سنی مختلف طراحی شوند و در ساعت های مناسب از شبکه های ملی و رسانه های عمومی پخش شوند تا با رده سنی مخاطب هماهنگ باشند.
مشارکت مردم
ایده های این تیزرها بهتر است از خود مردم گرفته شوند تا محتوا بر اساس نیازهای واقعی جامعه و مشکلات روزمره شکل بگیرد. استفاده از مدل crowd source می تواند کمک کند که این برنامه ها واقعی تر، کاربردی تر، و نزدیک تر به زندگی مردم باشند.

items.title: Repurposing Community Spaces: Transforming Mosques, Hosseiniehs, and Basij Bases into Early Learning and Community Centers
items.body:
Abstract
This proposal outlines a national initiative to repurpose underutilized or state-affiliated religious and paramilitary spaces—such as mosques, hosseiniehs, and former Basij facilities—into early childhood education centers and multifunctional community hubs.
The goal is to address critical gaps in early education, childcare access, and community infrastructure in post-transition Iran. By leveraging existing physical infrastructure, the project minimizes capital costs while rapidly delivering social impact.
These centers would provide:
•	Early childhood education (ages 2–6)
•	Parenting support programs
•	After-school activities
•	Community services and safe gathering spaces
Why It’s Interesting
Why now:
In a post-regime transition, Iran will face an urgent need to rebuild social trust, modernize education, and create inclusive community spaces. There will also be a large inventory of buildings requiring redefinition and reintegration into civilian life.
Why Iran:
Iran has a dense network of mosques, hosseiniehs, and Basij bases embedded within neighborhoods. These locations are:
•	Highly accessible
•	Structurally suitable for conversion
•	Symbolically important for community transformation
Expected Impact:
•	Rapid expansion of early childhood education access
•	Job creation (educators, caregivers, administrators)
•	Strengthening of local communities and social cohesion
•	Positive redefinition of previously politicized spaces
•	Long-term human capital development
Approach
Phase 1: Assessment & Planning (0–6 months)
•	Map and categorize eligible facilities nationwide
•	Assess structural integrity and suitability
•	Engage local communities for input and buy-in
•	Develop standardized design and conversion guidelines
Phase 2: Pilot Programs (6–18 months)
•	Launch pilot centers in major cities (e.g., Tehran, Shiraz, Isfahan)
•	Implement early learning curricula based on global best practices
•	Train educators and staff
•	Measure outcomes (enrollment, satisfaction, developmental metrics)
Phase 3: National Scale-Up (18–48 months)
•	Expand successful models across urban and rural regions
•	Establish public-private partnerships
•	Introduce digital systems for enrollment, monitoring, and quality control
Design Model Inspiration
Adapt proven community-centered models similar to those used in cities like
Toronto, where schools and community centers integrate:
•	Childcare
•	Recreation
•	Family services
•	Lifelong learning
⸻
Help Needed
Talent:
•	Early childhood education experts
•	Urban planners and architects
•	Community development specialists
•	Program managers
Funding:
•	International development grants
•	Philanthropic foundations
•	Impact investors
Partnerships:
•	NGOs focused on education and children
•	Diaspora professionals
•	Local municipalities and future civic institutions
Data & Research:
•	Demographic and geographic education needs
•	Facility mapping and infrastructure data
•	Best practices in early childhood development
Supporting Material (recommended)
•	Before/after architectural conversion concepts
•	Sample floor plans for early learning centers
•	Case studies from global cities (e.g., Toronto community hubs)
•	Visual diagrams of service integration (education + family support)
•	Pilot program metrics and dashboards
Goal Alignment
This initiative transforms existing infrastructure into high-impact social assets—creating scalable, cost-efficient, and community-driven solutions that can evolve into sustainable institutions and potentially private-public ventures.

items.title: Neighborhood Parcel Hubs & Smart Lockers
items.body:
Abstract
Improve last-mile delivery infrastructure in Iranian cities through a distributed network of local parcel hubs and automated lockers. This allows users to receive, send, and return packages without needing to be at home. The system combines physical service points (local shops or kiosks) with automated lockers.
Problem
E-commerce delivery in many Iranian cities lacks flexibility:

Deliveries can fail if the recipient is not home
Limited infrastructure for package pickup/drop-off outside major cities
Returns are inconvenient and sometimes unclear
Couriers waste time on repeated delivery attempts

Problem solved:
Introduce an intermediate delivery layer (local hubs + lockers) that decouples delivery from the recipient’s presence.
Why It's Interesting
Why now:

E-commerce in Iran is growing rapidly beyond major cities
Smartphone usage enables notification-based delivery systems
Increasing demand for flexible delivery options
Proven models exist globally

Why Iran:

Infrastructure gap between Tehran and smaller cities
Inefficiency in last-mile delivery
Local shops can act as low-cost service hubs (on a commission)

Expected impact:

Reduced failed deliveries
Better user experience for online shopping
Scalable for nationwide adoption
Lower environmental impact through optimized delivery routes and fewer repeated delivery attempts

Approach
Methods & Technology:

Smart lockers with secure code access
SMS-based notifications (low barrier to entry)
Mobile/web interface for users

Go-to-Market:

Phase 1: Target active online shoppers in one city
Phase 2: Partner with local delivery companies and small businesses
Phase 3: Expand through proven efficiency gains and user adoption

Notes

Can start without automation (manual hubs first)
Trust and reliability are key for adoption
Cultural habits (home delivery preference) should be considered
Long-term opportunity: integrate with national postal services

items.title: ♻️ Iran Recycling System
items.body:
♻️ Iran Recycling System — سیستم بازیافت ایران
A smart, scalable recycling infrastructure platform for Iran's 88-million-person market






🌍 The Opportunity — فرصت سرمایه‌گذاری

Iran generates 40+ million tons of waste per year — yet its recycling infrastructure remains fragmented, underfunded, and inaccessible to the public. That is not a problem. That is a market.

Iran has one of the largest untapped recycling markets in the Middle East. With a population of 88 million, rapid urbanization, and growing environmental awareness, the gap between waste produced and waste properly recycled represents a massive, largely unaddressed opportunity.
The Iran Recycling System is a bilingual (Persian/English), standards-based digital platform that bridges citizens, municipalities, and recycling centers — making the process of finding, sorting, and delivering recyclable materials as simple as opening an app.

🔥 Why Now — چرا همین الان؟



Signal
Detail




🏛️ Government pressure
Iran's Department of Environment has mandated waste reduction targets through 2030


📱 Mobile penetration
75%+ smartphone penetration across urban Iran


🌱 Public sentiment
Growing eco-consciousness among Iran's young, educated population (60% under 35)


💰 Resource economics
Recyclable materials (metals, PET, paper) carry significant resale value in Iranian markets


🚫 Zero digital competition
No dominant, consumer-facing recycling app exists in Iran today




🛠️ What We're Building — چه می‌سازیم؟

The platform is built on the Swiss Recycling Map standard (recycling-map.ch), adapted for Iranian cities, waste categories, and infrastructure.
Core Features

For Citizens

📍 Interactive map of recycling collection points across Iran
🗂️ 22-category waste sorting guide (paper, glass, electronics, hazardous, and more)
🔍 Search by city, district, or material type
🌐 Fully bilingual — Persian (RTL) and English
💡 Smart tips and reminders for responsible disposal

For Municipalities & Collection Centers

🖥️ Dashboard to manage accepted materials, hours, and capacity
📊 Analytics on collection volume and citizen engagement
🔔 Notifications for overflow or pickup scheduling

For Enterprises & NGOs

🤝 Corporate recycling program integration
📋 Compliance reporting tools aligned with Iran's environmental regulations
🔗 API access for third-party waste management systems


📐 Technical Foundation — پایه فنی
Stack: React / React Native · Node.js · PostgreSQL · REST API
Standards: Swiss Recycling Map (recycling-map.ch)
Languages: Persian (Farsi, RTL) + English
Deployment: Cloud-ready, scalable to national level

The codebase is modular, open-standards-based, and built from day one to scale from a single city pilot to a national infrastructure backbone.


📊 Market Size — اندازه بازار
Total Addressable Market (TAM)   →  88 million Iranians
Serviceable Market (SAM)         →  35 million urban smartphone users
Initial Target (SOM)             →  5 major cities: Tehran, Isfahan, Shiraz, Mashhad, Tabriz


Revenue streams include municipal licensing, enterprise recycling programs, data partnerships with environmental agencies, and premium features for collection center operators.


🗺️ Roadmap — نقشه راه

Phase 1 — Pilot (Months 1–6)

 Launch in Tehran with 50+ registered collection centers
 Onboard 3 municipal partners
 Reach 10,000 active users

Phase 2 — Expansion (Months 6–18)

 Scale to 5 major Iranian cities
 Launch enterprise recycling dashboard
 Integrate with national waste management API

Phase 3 — Platform (Months 18–36)

 Full national coverage
 Launch B2B marketplace for recyclable materials
 Regional expansion to neighboring markets (Afghanistan, Tajikistan — Persian-speaking)


🌊 Marine Recycling — بازیافت دریایی
Iran is bordered by three bodies of water — the Caspian Sea to the north, and the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman to the south. Each presents a distinct marine waste challenge, and each is an expansion opportunity for the platform.

🌍 Iran's Three Marine Zones



Sea / Gulf
Location
Key Concern




🌊 Caspian Sea
Northern Iran
World's largest enclosed lake — plastics with no ocean outlet


🐠 Persian Gulf
Southern Iran
Heavy shipping, oil infrastructure, coral reef degradation


🌀 Gulf of Oman
Southeast Iran
Fishing communities, ghost nets, cross-border marine waste




🧴 Marine Plastic & Waste Collection — جمع‌آوری پلاستیک دریایی
The Caspian Sea receives hundreds of thousands of tons of plastic waste annually from surrounding countries. Iran's Caspian coastline — covering Rasht, Babolsar, and Bandar Anzali — is among the most affected.
Platform features for marine plastic:

Coastal drop-off points mapped alongside inland recycling centers
Citizen reporting tool for illegal coastal dumping
Categorized collection for marine-grade plastics (salt-weathered, contaminated)
Partnership integration with port authorities and coastal municipalities



🛢️ Oil Spill Waste Management — مدیریت پسماند نفتی
The Persian Gulf is one of the world's busiest oil transit corridors. Iran operates major terminals at Kharg Island and Bandar Abbas. Oil spill waste — contaminated soil, absorbent materials, and sludge — requires specialist handling outside standard recycling chains.
Platform features for oil spill waste:

Dedicated hazardous marine waste category in the app
Registered specialist disposal centers near port cities (Bandar Abbas, Khorramshahr, Assaluyeh)
Compliance reporting tools for oil & gas operators
Incident reporting integration for coastal authorities


🎣 Fishing Net & Gear Recycling — بازیافت تور ماهیگیری
Ghost fishing gear — abandoned nets, lines, and traps — is among the most damaging forms of marine pollution. Iran has active fishing communities on all three coastlines, and discarded gear is a serious problem in both the Caspian and the Gulf of Oman.
Platform features for fishing gear:

Dedicated collection points at fishing ports and harbors
Net recycling program integration (nylon and polyester from nets recycled into new materials)
Incentive scheme for fishermen who return used gear
Tracking of recovered gear volume by port



📍 Key Coastal Cities in Scope



City
Coast
Marine Focus




Bandar Anzali
Caspian Sea
Plastic collection, industrial waste


Rasht
Caspian Sea
Urban runoff, coastal cleanup


Bandar Abbas

Oil waste, shipping debris

Persian Gulf
Fishing gear, port waste

Ghost nets, fishing communities




Iran's marine recycling program will be developed in Phase 2, running alongside the national city expansion. Coastal municipalities will be onboarded through the same platform infrastructure as inland cities.


💼 Investment Ask — درخواست سرمایه‌گذاری
We are raising a Seed round to fund:

Engineering team (mobile + backend)
Municipal partnerships and onboarding
Marketing and citizen adoption campaign
Regulatory compliance and legal groundwork


We are not building an app. We are building the digital infrastructure for Iran's recycling economy.

If you are an investor, development organization, environmental NGO, or municipality interested in a conversation, please reach out.
📧 Contact: Pedram.ghanavati[author].com

🌱 The Mission — ماموریت ما
In English: Every recycling system in the world started with a simple decision — to make it easy for people to do the right thing. Iran deserves that infrastructure. We are building it.

به فارسی: هر سیستم بازیافت موفقی در جهان با یک تصمیم ساده آغاز شد — آسان‌تر کردن کار درست برای مردم. ایران هم به این زیرساخت نیاز دارد. ما آن را می‌سازیم.


Built with 💚 for Iran · ساخته شده با عشق برای ایران
Based on Swiss Recycling Map standards

items.title: Standardized Addressing System Using Postal Codes & House Number
items.body:
Abstract
A nationwide effort to standardize address usage in Iran by promoting postal code-based identification. Instead of long, inconsistent textual addresses (X square, after Y cross, next to Z store, etc.), users can rely on a short, structured format (postal code + house number) to uniquely identify locations. This improves delivery, navigation, and digital services.
Problem
Although Iran has a 10-digit postal code system, it is underutilized:

People rely on long, non-standard address descriptions
Address formats vary widely between individuals and platforms
Many users do not know or trust their postal codes
Delivery services often require additional clarification
Digital systems lack a unified addressing standard

Problem solved:
Replace ambiguous textual addressing with a reliable, standardized system.
Why It's Interesting
Why now:

Growth of e-commerce and delivery services
Increased reliance on digital services (maps, ride-hailing, logistics)
Existing infrastructure (postal codes) already in place

Why Iran:

High inefficiency in last-mile delivery
Frequent address ambiguity and errors
Opportunity to modernize national infrastructure
Strong synergy with logistics, e-commerce, and smart city initiatives

Expected impact:

Shorter, clearer addresses
Fewer delivery errors
Faster logistics operations
Improved mapping and navigation services
Foundation for future smart city systems

Approach
Steps
Awareness & Education:

Public campaigns to encourage use of postal codes
Tools to easily find postal codes

Platform Integration:

Require postal code fields in e-commerce and delivery apps
Auto-fill address based on postal code

Standardization:

Define a simple format: Postal Code + House Number
Encourage adoption across services

Incentives:

Faster/cheaper delivery for standardized addresses
Priority handling for complete postal code usage

Timeline
Initial adoption: 6 months
Widespread platform integration: 12 months
Cultural normalization: 1–2 years
Methods & Technology

Postal code database integration APIs
Address auto-completion systems
Mobile apps/web tools for lookup
Integration with maps and delivery platforms

Go-to-Market

Phase 1: Partner with e-commerce and delivery services
Phase 2: Integrate with government and postal services
Phase 3: Nationwide adoption through standardization

Help Needed

GIS / mapping specialists
Backend developers (API + database)
Government / postal service collaboration
UX designers for simple address input

Notes

Cultural habits may resist change initially
Must ensure high accuracy of postal code database

items.title: Exponential Food Security System for Iran: A Protein-First Approach
items.body:
Abstract
The first issue any country must solve is food security.
No one should sleep hungry, and minimum daily food access should be treated as a basic right.
This idea focuses on protein supply as a key national priority and proposes a scalable, exponential food-production system built around natural biological converters and fast-growth species.
Why It’s Interesting
Iran needs solutions that are practical, scalable, and realistic under water and resource constraints.
Instead of trying to solve everything at once, this model starts from the most urgent layer: feeding people efficiently and affordably.
The system can begin with:

high-protein plants
black soldier fly larvae for converting waste into animal feed protein
fast-growth species such as quail
gradual expansion into fish, poultry, and livestock

This is not just theoretical. Parts of this logic are already being tested in pilot form in the UAE, including rapid growth models in quail production.
Approach
The goal is to build a step-by-step national food chain based on exponential scaling:

Start with the fastest and most efficient protein pathways
Convert waste into feed inputs where possible
Expand from animal feed protein into human food protein
Gradually diversify into other livestock, fish, and low-water agricultural systems
Replicate this model through provincial hubs over time

A realistic point is that in the first years, Iran does not need to insist on producing every carbohydrate crop domestically, especially where water costs are too high. Some parts of the chain can be imported temporarily while domestic protein and resilience systems are built properly.
Help Needed

feedback on system design
provincial scaling ideas
agricultural and livestock expertise
water-efficient crop suggestions
partnerships for pilot hubs

Supporting Note
For better understanding, I have added a more detailed explanation in the comment below.

items.title: National Earthquake Resilience Program (Buildings & Heritage Sites)
items.body:
Abstract
This idea proposes a nationwide program to systematically improve earthquake resilience across both residential buildings and cultural heritage sites in Iran. The program needs to combine engineering solutions, regulation, and international collaboration to significantly reduce future disaster damage.
Problem
Iran is highly earthquake-prone, yet:

Many existing buildings are not earthquake-resistant
Enforcement of construction standards is inconsistent
Cultural heritage sites are extremely vulnerable
Past disasters have caused massive human and economic loss

Problem solved:
Reduce structural vulnerability before disasters happen, rather than reacting afterward.
Why It's Interesting
Why now:

Recent earthquakes in the region (e.g., Turkey, 2023) show systemic vulnerability
Urban populations are growing rapidly
Engineering solutions for retrofitting already exist
Disaster prevention is far cheaper than reconstruction

Why Iran:

Located on major seismic fault lines
Large stock of older, vulnerable buildings
High-value cultural heritage at risk
Strong need for national-level coordination

Expected impact:

Significant reduction in casualties during earthquakes
Lower economic losses
Increased public safety and trust
Protection of cultural identity and heritage
Improved long-term urban resilience

Approach
Steps:
Phase 1: Assessment

Nationwide structural risk assessment
Identify high-risk residential zones
Prioritize critical infrastructure and dense urban areas

Phase 2: Retrofitting Existing Buildings

Apply modern engineering techniques to reinforce structures
Provide financial incentives or subsidies for homeowners
Focus first on high-risk regions

Phase 3: New Construction Standards (Immediate + Ongoing)

Enforce strict earthquake- and fire-resistance regulations
Mandatory inspections and compliance checks
Transparent certification system

Phase 4: Heritage Protection

Reinforce historical sites using specialized techniques
Collaborate with international experts
Balance preservation with structural safety

Phase 5: International Collaboration

Partner with experts from countries like Japan
Transfer knowledge and best practices
Joint research and training programs

Methods & Technology

Structural retrofitting techniques (steel bracing, base isolation, fiber reinforcement)
Fire-resistant materials and design standards
Seismic monitoring and risk mapping
Engineering audits and certification systems

Go-to-Market
Phase 1: Government-led pilot in high-risk cities
Phase 2: Public-private partnerships for scaling retrofits
Phase 3: Nationwide regulation and enforcement
Help Needed

Structural engineers
Urban planners
Government and regulatory bodies
International experts (e.g., Japan)
Funding and financing mechanisms

Notes

High upfront cost but massive long-term savings
Requires strong governance and enforcement
Public awareness and trust are critical
Heritage preservation must balance safety and authenticity

Interoperability across banks and apps

This combination transforms both how money moves and what money is:

Real-time + final settlement

Expands financial inclusion at scale

Fragmented & Delayed Settlement: instant, final settlement
Cash Handling Complexity: Printing, transporting, storing, reconciling cash
Reconciliation Overhead: Banks reconcile balances faster
Liquidity Lock-up: reduce idle capital requirements
Limited Control Over Money Behavior: programmable (rules, conditions, expiry)
Offline & Access Gaps

Billions of transactions monthly
Universal QR acceptance (even street vendors)
Reducing reliance on cards
Reducing cost of printing banknotes
ATM infrastructure
Cash logistics
Better Security & reconciliation

User scans QR / enters phone number
App sends request

items.title: Empowering autistic individuals, people with Down syndrome through meaningful, dignified work in document digitization. Extracting historical data from documents using LLMs.
items.body:
Empowering autistic individuals, people with Down syndrome, through meaningful, dignified work in document digitization. Extracting historical data from documents using LLMs.
[author removed]


Erfan Ghasemi, PhD in Biostatistics, Senior Data Scientist

ghasemi.erfan[author].com
LinkedIn



Mabby Akhlaghi, PhD in Biostatistics, Data Scientist

mah1akhlaghi[author].com
LinkedIn




Abstract
What it is
Unfortunately, over the past 47 years, some groups---such as individuals with autism---have not always had equal opportunities to participate in the workforce. Many autistic individuals can develop deep focus and exceptional skills in areas they are passionate about. For example, someone with a strong interest in music may achieve a very high level of expertise.
It would be valuable to identify each person's strengths and interests, and then connect them with meaningful job opportunities that align with those abilities.
One promising opportunity we've identified is working with large volumes of documents across different fields. This could involve taking photos of documents and using an application to digitize them and extract key information. Such a role can be structured, focused, and well-suited to individuals who enjoy detail-oriented tasks, while also creating real value through organized data and insights.
We can extend it for people with Down Syndrome, as well.

Why It Matters
Two major problems exist in parallel in Iran and are rarely connected:
Autistic people, and individuals with Down syndrome face unemployment rates that are high and society has not accepted them over the years.

Digitizing, extracting and utilizing historical data is essential for gaining valuable insights.


The Problem Solved
Millions of businesses in Iran hold years of undigitized paper records. Converting these to digital format is time-consuming, repetitive, and requires careful attention to detail, but not deep cognitive concentration. This makes it a uniquely ideal job for neurodivergent individuals whose natural strengths include:

High accuracy and consistency in repetitive work
Strong focus and dedication when engaged in the right environment


Why Now – Why Iran

Iran is going to connect with the global economy and free market, necessitating competition with companies worldwide.
Demand for document digitization will grow as companies will face regulatory and tax compliance requirements.
There is increasing global and local awareness around disability rights and inclusive employment.
Technological advancements like smartphones, OCR, and cloud storage have made high-quality document scanning more accessible and affordable. Additionally, with the regime change and lifting of sanctions, we will have unrestricted access to fast LLMs and AI services.
A large, underserved population of autistic and disabled individuals with no structured employment pathways.


Expected Impact



Impact Area
Expected Outcome




Social
10–30 neurodivergent workers employed in Year 1, with plans to scale


Economic
Affordable digitization services for SMEs, accounting firms, hospitals, and law offices


Psychological
Increased dignity, purpose, and social inclusion for workers and their families


Scalability
Replicable model that can be expanded to other cities and document types in Year 2+




Key Steps

Step 1: Talent Interview & Assessment
Step 2: Training Program
Step 3: Operations
Step 4: Designing applications and AI agents for Persian-language documents, tailored to specific industries, to extract key insights and actionable information. (Already we have an application for English Finance Documents)


Help Needed



Category
Details




Talent
Job coaches and social workers; psychologists experienced with autism and Down syndrome; HR professionals with inclusive hiring experience


Funding
Impact investors, social enterprise grants, Iranian Welfare Organization (Sazman Behzisti), and international NGOs focused on disability inclusion


Technology
Mobile app developer for the document scanning interface; cloud storage and OCR integration specialists


Partnerships
Autism associations, rehabilitation organizations


Data & Compliance
Legal advisors for data privacy laws in Iran; secure document handling protocols and NDA frameworks for clients





Timeline: 6 months

items.title: Animal Control System For Stray Dogs and Cats
items.body:
In Iran, stray animals are a significant part of the ecosystem. Unfortunately, due to a lack of education and proper care systems, they are often abused, injured, improperly fed, or even killed. Poor nutrition, inadequate or nonexistent care, and the absence of effective population control not only harm these animals but also make them a potential risk to other species and, in some cases, to children. Therefore, there is a critical need for a structured system to protect these animals, which in turn helps protect the broader environment. Such a system falls under multiple key sectors, including environmental management, public health, legal and regulatory frameworks, social and community support, and municipal services . Modern countries typically use a mix of animal control services, public policy, and nonprofit partnerships to manage stray dogs and cats in a humane and sustainable way. The most effective systems are not just about “removing” animals, but creating a full ecosystem of care, control, and adoption.
My idea is to develop a hybrid animal care system that combines elements of both the Turkey and United States models. This approach would allow animals to remain free-roaming but within a structured and managed framework.
To break it down, the system would include:
1.	Nationwide access to free spay and neuter services
2.	Mandatory microchipping for all pets
3.	Trap–Neuter–Return (TNR) programs combined with vaccination for stray animals
4.	Government-funded, no-kill shelters
5.	Strong adoption and foster care networks
6.	Public education initiatives, which would play a critical role
7.	Strict laws against animal abandonment
This is a multi-sector economy around animal welfare
That impacts:
•	Public health
•	Technology innovation
•	Community engagement
I do not have formal education in this field, and I recognize that there are likely more effective or refined ways to implement such a system. So I would greatly appreciate any feedback or suggestions for improvement.

items.body:
ایده: احیای فرهنگ‌های  ملی و محلی ایران
ایران یکی از غنی‌ترین فرهنگ‌های جهان را دارد، اما بسیاری از رقص‌ها، غذاها، دسرها و سنت‌های محلی در حال فراموش شدن هستند و حتی خود ما ایرانی‌ها هم بسیاری از آن‌ها را نمی‌شناسیم.
پیشنهاد: ایجاد یک پروژه ملی با چند بخش مکمل.
فستیوال‌های گردشی سالانه
یک فستیوال فرهنگی که در طول سال، شهر به شهر حرکت کند و در مرکز هر استان برگزار شود. در هر فستیوال اجرای رقص‌های محلی از سراسر ایران، غرفه‌های غذا، دسر و شیرینی از شهرهای مختلف و نمایش فرهنگ‌ها در کنار هم وجود دارد. نکته کلیدی این است که مردم هر شهر بتوانند «کل ایران» را در شهر خودشان تجربه کنند.
اجراهای زنده رقص (مدل کنسرت)
ایجاد یک لوکیشن مشخص، مثلاً در تهران، برای اجرای دائمی و حرفه‌ای رقص‌های محلی ایران. اجراها برنامه‌ریزی‌شده و باکیفیت هستند، امکان خرید بلیط مانند کنسرت وجود دارد و مناسب برای عموم مردم و گردشگران است. این بخش می‌تواند به یک تجربه ثابت فرهنگی تبدیل شود، به‌طوری که حضور در این اجراها به بخشی از برنامه سفر گردشگران به ایران تبدیل شود.
برنامه تلویزیونی مستمر (نه مقطعی)
یک برنامه شاد، مفرح و فرهنگی که به‌صورت پیوسته  پخش شود، نه محدود به یک فصل یا یک سال. فرمت می‌تواند برنامه سیزنال باشد یا آیتم‌های کوتاه بین برنامه‌ها. محتوای هر قسمت شامل معرفی یک شهر یا استان، رقص‌های محلی، غذاها، دسرها و شیرینی‌های سنتی و لباس‌ها و آیین‌های فرهنگی است. هدف این است که مردم ایران به‌صورت مداوم با فرهنگ یکدیگر آشنا شوند، نه فقط در یک بازه کوتاه.
نتیجه
این پروژه می‌تواند به یک جریان فرهنگی زنده و مداوم تبدیل شود، نه فقط یک برنامه، بلکه یک تجربه ملی و ماندگار. فرهنگ اگر دیده نشود، به مرور از بین می‌رود. این ایده تلاش می‌کند فرهنگ ایران را زنده، جاری و قابل تجربه نگه دارد

items.title: The Arc of Stability
items.body:
Since most Middle Eastern countries are Islamic, and therefore Islamism is rooted within their societies, in a future Iran it would make sense to establish a cooperation pact or even an alliance with those Middle Eastern countries that are geographically important but non-Islamic. In other words, an alliance that is completely the opposite of the Islamic Republic’s Axis of Resistance.
This alliance could include: Iran, Israel, Armenia, Georgia, and Cyprus.
I will explain my reasoning for each of them below.
Why do I think this idea is good?
1.	Most of the Middle East’s regional crises are ideological (political Islam, pan Arabism, pan Turkism).
2.	A new Iran, being secular, nation-state oriented, and economically driven is inherently incompatible with that environment. Therefore, if Iran defines itself within a bloc that is non-ideological, non Islamic, state centered, and pragmatic:
•	Regional friction costs would decrease
•	Alliances would become more stable
•	Iran could become the natural leader of this bloc due to its population, history, and geopolitical position.
These countries could align with Iran, and their alliance would be meaningful:

Israel
•	Non-Islamic
•	Technologically advanced
•	Security-oriented
•	A perfect complement to Iran (energy ↔ technology ↔ security)

An Iran–Israel alliance = a fundamental shift in the region’s balance of power.

Armenia
•	Non-Islamic
•	Dependent on Iranian transit routes
•	Strongly in need of economic growth.

Iran could become Armenia’s strategic supporter.


Georgia
•	Secular
•	Pro-Western
•	Opposed to Russian influence
•	A bridge from the Caucasus to the Black Sea
Vital for connecting Iran to Europe.


Cyprus
•	Non-Islamic
•	Member of the European Union
•	A natural partner of Israel and Europe


A key position in the Eastern Mediterranean
Multi layered cooperation framework:
1.	Maritime and cyber security
2.	Transit, economy and energy
3.	Technology and defense
4.	Countering extremism
Direct geopolitical effects:
1.	Breaking the ideological axis in the region:
The center of gravity would shift from religion/ethnicity/ideology to nation-state/interests.
2.	Connecting three strategic zones:
•	Persian Gulf → Iranian plateau → Caucasus → Mediterranean → Europe
3.	Containing pan-ideologies without war
4.	Enhancing Iran’s role
5.	Facilitating investment and supply chains
Joint transnational projects:
•	Energy (gas, electricity, hydrogen)
•	Transit and corridors
•	Technology, cyber, and defense industrial sectors
Objectives:
1.	Gradual creation of a common market
2.	Ensuring regional connectivity and energy flows
3.	Strengthening collective security cooperation
4.	Promoting investment, innovation, and technology exchange
5.	Preventing ideological, religious, or ethnic destabilization
6.	Joint development of pipelines, power grids, ports, and corridors
7.	Protecting critical infrastructure as a shared security priority
8.	Gradual removal of tariffs and non-tariff barriers
9.	Free flow of capital and skilled labor
Key message to the world:
This alliance would be a stabilizing force that creates economic interdependence, secures trade routes, and neutralizes ideological extremism without military escalation.
Core features of this alliance:
•	Complementary to Western security architecture
•	Reduces the need for U.S. or European intervention in the region
•	Strengthens energy security and supply chains
•	Market-driven, rules-based, and transparent

items.title: Constitute Iran Energy Regulator
items.body:
Mandate


Provide for the safe, efficient, orderly, and environmentally responsible development of oil and gas resources, including protection of air, land, water, and biodiversity.
Regulate the full lifecycle of projects: from application and construction through operation, suspension, abandonment, and closure.
Balance environmental protection, public safety, and economic benefits in the interest of all people in the country.


Scope and functions


Single regulator for upstream and midstream oil and gas (wells, facilities, pipelines, processing plants, storage, and related water and land use for these activities).
Core functions: application review, environmental and social impact assessment, licensing and approvals, monitoring and inspection, enforcement, and site closure requirements.
Administer and apply sector‑specific environment, water, land, and remediation laws for oil and gas activities, under overarching environment and natural resources legislation.


Governance and independence


Statutory corporation created by an energy development act, with its own legal personality, powers, and duties defined in law.
Independent board of directors responsible for strategy and oversight; separate hearing commissioners or panels for quasi‑judicial decisions on applications and disputes.
Accountable to government for alignment with legislation and policy, but operationally independent in individual regulatory decisions.


Environmental and social protection tools


Mandatory environmental impact assessments for major projects, including cumulative effects, mitigation plans, and emergency response plans.
Clear regulatory requirements on emissions, flaring, spills, water use, contamination management, remediation, and reclamation, with detailed technical standards and guidelines.
Lifecycle liability management: financial and operational requirements to ensure companies properly close, remediate, and reclaim sites.


Compliance, enforcement, and transparency


Risk‑based inspections and audits, with a range of enforcement tools (orders, penalties, licence suspensions, shutdowns).
Duty to publish key regulatory requirements, applications, decisions, and bulletins so industry and the public understand expectations.
Regular performance reporting on how well the regulator is meeting its mandate and managing environmental and safety risks.

items.title: Advanced Road Marking & Lane Guidance System
items.body:
Abstract
Redoing road marking system that goes beyond basic lane separation. It introduces early lane guidance, consistent visual language, and additional marking types (e.g., bus lanes, merging guides, hazard zones). By learning from successful implementations in countries like the Netherlands, the system improves safety and efficiency.

Problem
In many Iranian cities:

Lane boundaries are unclear or faded
Drivers make last-second lane changes
Turning lanes are not clearly indicated in advance
Limited use of advanced markings (e.g., merge guides, dedicated lanes)
Traffic flow becomes unpredictable and unsafe

Problem solved:
Create a complete visual guidance on the road that makes driving behavior more predictable and structured.
Why It's Interesting
Why now:

Increasing traffic congestion
High rate of avoidable accidents
Proven success of road marking systems globally
Low cost compared to building new roads (for now)

Why Iran:

Inconsistency in road design and markings
Immediate improvement potential with minimal infrastructure change
Strong need for better traffic discipline without heavy enforcement

Expected impact:

Reduced sudden lane changes
Fewer accidents at intersections and merges
Smoother traffic flow
Improved driver confidence and predictability
Lower stress and cognitive load for drivers
Better utilization of existing road capacity

Approach
Steps
- Evaluate current marking quality and gaps
- Design Standardization (Lane separation, Early directional arrows, dedicated turn lanes, etc.)
- Pilot Implementation
- Scaling
- International Benchmarking ( Study and adapt best practices from countries like the Netherlands and other high-performing road systems and then localize standards based on Iranian driving behavior and infrastructure)
Notes

Cost-effective compared to infrastructure expansion
Requires maintenance to remain visible and effective
Should be combined with driver education and light enforcement
Can significantly improve behavior even without strict policing

items.title: Why English Education Is Important
items.body:
In our country, many people have a big weakness in English. I think more than 95% of people cannot speak or understand English well. This makes it hard for them to learn new things, find better jobs, and communicate with people from other countries.
One possible solution is to follow the example of India. In India, many schools and universities teach courses in English. Because of this, many Indian people can speak English and work with international companies.
I think our country should also move in this direction. For example, all courses in schools and universities can be taught in English. This change should not happen suddenly. It can be done step by step over a period of about 10 years.
Also, teachers are very important in this process. We should train current teachers to improve their English skills. But if some teachers cannot speak English even after training, we may need to replace them with teachers who can speak English fluently. This will help students learn better.
If we improve English education, our country can become more successful. People can get better jobs, especially in international companies. They can also communicate with people around the world, share ideas, and learn new skills.
In my opinion, this change can increase our country’s growth and development. It can help us become more active in the global economy and improve our future.

items.title: Giving Opportunities to Returning Immigrants
items.body:
When people immigrate to another country, they get new experience and skills. After some time, some of them may want to come back to their home country.
I think these people should have a chance to return to their previous jobs. If they want to work again in their old job, they should have this opportunity.
These people can help our country because they learned new things in other countries. They can bring new ideas, better skills, and international experience.
This can help companies grow and improve. It can also help the country develop faster.
In my opinion, giving this chance is good for both people and the country.

items.title: VoteChain – A secure, privacy-preserving digital voting system using blockchain and anonymous tokens.
items.body:
VoteChain
Privacy-Preserving Blockchain Voting System
Overview
This project proposes a two-layer digital voting system that combines identity verification with anonymous, token-based voting on a blockchain.
The system is designed to ensure:

One person = one vote
Strong voter privacy
Public verifiability
Tamper-resistant vote storage

Votes are recorded immutably on a blockchain such as Ethereum, while identity verification is handled separately to preserve anonymity.

Motivation
Why this matters
Traditional voting systems face challenges such as:

Lack of transparency
Risk of manipulation
Limited accessibility for remote voters

This system addresses these issues by leveraging:

Blockchain for transparency and immutability
Token-based voting for single-use ballots
Separation of identity and voting for privacy

Why now

Advances in blockchain technology
Increasing demand for digital governance
Growing distrust in centralized systems

Why Iran (Use Case)

Need for transparent and verifiable systems
Potential for secure diaspora participation
High adoption potential among tech-savvy population


Architecture
The system is divided into two main layers:
1. Identity Layer

Users verify identity via a third-party provider (passport + face verification)
The third-party stores only:

passport_hash → registered (yes/no)


After approval:
A random UserID is generated (256-bit)
A random username is assigned
No personal data is stored in the voting system


2. Voting Layer (Token Pool System)
Election Initialization

Count eligible users: N
Generate N random voting tokens
Publish on blockchain:
Number of eligible users
Number of generated tokens

Token Pool

Tokens are stored securely:

TokenID
status: unused / reserved / used


Accessible only through internal APIs


Voting Process

User logs in with pseudonymous account
User requests a voting token
System assigns a random unused token
User submits vote:

Token + VoteChoice


Token is marked as used (cannot be reused)


Blockchain Layer
Votes are recorded on-chain:

Token → Vote

Optional Enhancement
For increased privacy:


Token → EncryptedVote


This ensures:

Immutable vote records
Public auditability
Protection against double voting




Privacy Model



Component
Knows Identity
Knows Vote




Identity Provider
Yes
No


Voting System
No
Yes


Blockchain
No
Yes



No single component can link a voter to their vote.

Security Considerations

Single-use tokens prevent double voting
Token pool ensures controlled vote issuance
Blockchain ensures immutability
API-only access protects internal databases

Future Improvements

Encrypted voting (end-to-end encryption)
Threshold key management
Homomorphic vote tallying
Zero-knowledge proofs

Reduces long-term fuel costs

💸 4. Competitive Cost Structure
Lower labor costs
Lower engineering and construction costs
🌐 5. Strategic Location
Bridge between regions
Access to northern & southern corridors
Potential for regional data flow
⚙️ Core Concept: Hybrid Energy-Powered Data Centers
Instead of relying only on the grid, build integrated systems:
🔥 Gas → Reliability (base load)
☀️ Solar → Cost reduction

A system that is:
Reliable
Cost-efficient
Scalable
Less dependent on the grid

Dust & Soiling


Major issue in Iran, Iraq, Saudi, Sahara regions

Needed for:


Panel cleaning
Data center cooling

Solar
Gas
Data centers

Iran has a rare combination of:
Cheap energy
Available land
Strategic geography

items.title: Political and governmental systems teachings as an essential foundation for fair referendums and elections
items.body:
Teaching the public about all possible political and governmental systems during the transition period through unbiased media in all formats so that all voters are reached and informed.
If there's to be fair referendums and/or elections after the fall of the Islamic Republic to choose a type of government, the public needs to be completely informed and aware of all the possible choices and their consequences in all aspects of life and future. This is an essential part of foundation of a prosperous future for Iran.
What comes to my mind is somewhat like the Swiss referendum system, where all voters are sent extensive materials about the subjects of the referendum, which includes pros and cons of both yes and no scenarios to the referendum.
These informative materials must include answers to questions like:
how is the constitution reformed?
how does each governmental system work?
Is it a federal or state government? what does that even mean?
what falls under which jurisdiction?
how does a parliament formed?
how are laws passed?
Is it a direct or semi-direct democracy? what does that even mean?
how would the healthcare system and education system look like in each governmental systems?
how are freedoms of speech, religion and press are affected by each governmental systems?
what are the guidelines against extremism for each governmental systems?
and so on and so forth.
everything must be explained in a way that is understandable for the public who are not expert in that area. All governmental systems must include historical and present examples and pros and cons of each must be explained in detail and context.
I am not a social or political scientist nor an expert in economics or law.
Easy access to unbiased and trustworthy and unnecessarily complicated information in Farsi and all major languages spoken in Iran, like Kurdi, Azeri, Luri, Arabic and much more, is something I long hoped for the people of Iran.
I'd suggest unbiased experts and educators that have no affiliations to any current or future parties to help in this matter.

items.title: Rebuilding education in Iran for a modern future
items.body:
Iran’s education system needs more than reform; it needs a full rebuild.
Right now, the structure and curriculum are heavily shaped by ideological and religious frameworks, which limit critical thinking, creativity, and real-world readiness. Students spend years memorizing instead of learning how to think, question, build, and apply knowledge.
The idea is to redesign education from the ground up into a modern, secular, and application-driven system. Something closer to globally aligned models like inquiry-based and project-based learning, where students actually engage with concepts instead of repeating them. Systems similar to IB-style education come to mind, where learning is interdisciplinary, practical, and connected to real-world problems.
At the core of this is a full curriculum redesign, moving away from ideology-driven content toward science-based, critical thinking–focused education. Subjects should be more interconnected, blending math, science, technology, and real-life applications instead of being taught in isolation.
Technology should be a core part of this rebuild, not an add-on. AI can support personalized learning paths, adaptive pacing, and scalable tutoring. A strong national online learning infrastructure could make high-quality education accessible across the country, especially in underserved areas, through a hybrid model that combines in-person and digital learning.
Another key part is teachers. A transformation like this only works if educators are supported and retrained in modern teaching methods. This isn’t about replacing teachers; it’s about giving them better tools, better frameworks, and ongoing development so they can actually guide students through meaningful learning.
There’s also an opportunity to align more closely with global education systems, allowing students to transition more easily into international universities and careers, while still building something that fits Iran’s context.
Iran already has incredibly talented students and educators. The problem isn’t capability, it’s the system. If redesigned correctly, education could become one of the fastest ways to rebuild the country’s future across science, technology, the economy, and global collaboration.
This kind of transformation would need collaboration across multiple areas, from curriculum designers and educators to engineers, AI developers, and international education experts, along with funding and long-term partnerships. There are already strong global examples, frameworks, and tools that can be adapted and built upon rather than starting from scratch.
Background: I’m a chemical engineer with about a decade of experience in education across K–12, undergraduate, and graduate levels, including curriculum development, online learning systems, and AI-supported training. This idea comes directly from both academic and practical experience working with different education models.

items.title: IranID: A National Mobile e-ID and Digital Signature Platform for Iran
items.body:
Turn Iran’s existing national ID base into IranID, a single nationwide mobile identity and digital-signature system for government, banking, healthcare, education, and business.
Why Iran:
• ~92.4M population
• ~86.8% mobile-phone ownership
• ~96.8% LTE/WiMAX population coverage
• Sweden’s BankID reached 8.7M unique users in 2025, showing how powerful one shared e-ID can become
What it looks like:
• One secure mobile identity app
• One accepted digital-signature standard
• One API used by banks, ministries, insurers, telecoms, and universities
• Integrated access to payments, forms, contracts, prescriptions, and permits
Why this works:
• Iran already has the core identity and telecom foundation
• The main gap is fragmentation, not lack of users
• A unified e-ID sharply reduces fraud, paperwork, and in-person verification
Impact:
• Faster services, lower costs, less fraud
• Better digital access across the country
• Foundation for a modern digital economy and state capacity.
Approach:

define a legal and technical standard for digital identity, authentication, and signatures that can be accepted across banks, ministries, telecoms, and regulated private services.
launch a secure mobile app linked to the national identity registry, using PIN, biometrics, and device binding.
provide API access so banks, hospitals, universities, insurers, and government portals can integrate a single login and signing flow.
expand use cases to include account opening, tax filing, permits, prescriptions, education records, business registration, and contract signing.
add resilience features such as low-bandwidth mode, assisted verification, and offline fallback for weak-connectivity areas.
A realistic rollout would start with a 12-month pilot in a few high-demand sectors, followed by 2–3 years of national scaling.

Help Needed:
Identity and security engineers, mobile developers, cryptography experts, legal/regulatory advisors, banking and telecom partners, UX designers, public-sector digitization teams, pilot institutions, and funding for platform development, audits, and integration support. Access to anonymized service-flow data would also help prioritize the first high-impact integrations.

items.title: Lessons from the French System
items.body:
درود بر تمام شما
I've had the chance to experience the French education system firsthand, and some of what I saw genuinely impressed me, not as a perfect model, but as one with ideas worth borrowing, especially for a country like Iran.
One thing that stands out right away is how early schooling begins. French children start at three years old, in a structured environment called maternelle. Beyond giving parents more flexibility, it gives kids early exposure to learning and socializing, something I think makes a real difference down the line.
By secondary school, students aren't all pushed down the same path. They can choose between general, technological, or vocational tracks based on their actual interests and strengths. Speaking of vocational education, it's treated with genuine respect in France. Working with your hands isn't seen as a fallback option. That attitude matters more than people realize.
But the thing I keep coming back to is the mandatory PHILOSOPHY course in the final year. Every student takes it, regardless of their track. It teaches you that most hard questions don't have a single right answer, that certainty is often an illusion, and that disagreement doesn't have to mean conflict. Honestly, I think this kind of training is one of the best safeguards against radicalization there is.
Then there's laïcité ,the strict secular neutrality of public schools. No religious instruction, no proselytism, no symbols that divide. Just a shared space built around reason and citizenship. If I had to pick one principle to introduce in Iranian schools first, it would be this one.
One thing I genuinely appreciated is that French high school doesn't feel like a pressure cooker. Students aren't constantly ranked against each other or pushed to prove themselves through relentless competition. That intense drive, the kind that defines who gets ahead, tends to kick in later, at the university level and beyond, when young people are actually ready to choose it for themselves. High school is more about building a foundation than winning a race. I think that's a healthier way to grow up.
None of this works, of course, without good teachers, well-paid, well-supported, and genuinely respected. That's the foundation everything else rests on.
The French system has real flaws and ongoing struggles. But its core ideas, early access, philosophy for all, secularism, and dignity for every kind of work, are worth taking seriously. You don't have to copy the whole thing to benefit from the best parts.

items.title: Independent AI in national leadership
items.body:
Independent AI in national leadership
AI as an impartial overseer: It reviews laws, policies, budgets, and executive decisions — stepping in or vetoing anything that clashes with the constitution, human rights, or international treaties.
Semi-autonomous governance: AI handles major resource allocation, economic policies, national security choices, or routine judicial rulings on its own, based purely on data, logic, and set long-term goals — no constant human micromanagement.
Advisory or executive role: Think of an independent "AI Council" acting as top advisor or even taking executive steps to shield decisions from bias, corruption, short-term populism, or emotional errors — always prioritizing evidence and the nation's future.
Crisis command: In disasters, pandemics, or security threats, AI delivers fast, calm, optimized responses — coordinating rescues, predicting spread, allocating aid — without human panic or hesitation.

items.title: Integrated North-West Corridor: Energy, Connectivity, and Green Transition
items.body:
The North-West Strategic Infrastructure Ribbon (NWS-IR)
One Route, Triple Value: Energy, Connectivity, and Green Transition

The "Ribbon" Strategy: A Unified Infrastructure Core
Unlike traditional, siloed projects, the NWS-IR focuses on the development of a Unified Infrastructure Ribbon. By securing a single Right-of-Way (ROW) for three distinct industries—Energy, Data, and Logistics—the project achieves a 40% reduction in capital expenditure (CAPEX) and maximizes land-use efficiency across the Iran-Armenia-Georgia transit route.
Triple-Layer Architecture (The Corridor’s Anatomy)
The Ribbon consists of three integrated operational layers moving within a single protected perimeter:


Layer A (Energy): A high-pressure, Hydrogen-Ready gas pipeline designed for immediate natural gas export, with the metallurgical integrity to transition into a 100% Green Hydrogen carrier for the European market.
Layer B (Digital): An ultra-high-capacity Fiber-Optic Backbone providing the shortest overland route from the East to Europe. This layer features "Cold-Node" data center clusters strategically located in high-altitude, low-temperature regions like Ardabil to minimize cooling costs.
Layer C (Logistics): A high-speed Electrified Rail Link connecting Persian Gulf logistics hubs to Georgian Black Sea ports (Poti/Batumi), serving as a faster, terrestrial alternative to the Suez Canal.


Strategic Impact: The Gateway to European Resilience
The NWS-IR is designed to solve three critical geopolitical challenges:


Energy Diversification: Providing the EU with a reliable, terrestrial source of both transitional gas and future-state Green Hydrogen.
Digital Latency: Reducing global data latency by bypassing the vulnerable and congested maritime routes of the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.
Climate Leadership: Establishing the region's first Decarbonized Transit Corridor, powered by integrated solar farms along the route's arid stretches.


Implementation Pillars
The project will be managed by a Private Infrastructure Holding company focusing on:


Consolidated Permitting: Securing tri-national "Common Corridor" agreements (Iran-Armenia-Georgia) for a streamlined regulatory environment.
Modular Construction: Implementing simultaneous trenching and laying of pipeline and fiber to accelerate the ROI cycle.
Smart Hub Integration: Transforming transit stops into Special Economic Zones (SEZs) for hydrogen electrolysis and automated freight handling.


Immediate Requirements


Tri-National Diplomatic Accord: Finalizing a framework for a "Joint Sovereignty Corridor" to protect long-term investments.
Geological & Technical Audit: Comprehensive seismic and soil stability analysis to ensure the safety of co-located rail and high-pressure gas lines.
Infrastructure Investment Vehicle (IIV): Formation of a private consortium to manage multi-stage funding and international transit treaties.

items.title: Coordinated request for Community Notes on X
items.body:
Abstract: Community Notes carry greater weight than replies in response to posts on X that attempt to obstruct, delay, or reverse the current geopolitical momentum in Iran toward freedom. A coordinated effort to request Community Notes on certain high-profile posts can assist in challenging propaganda.
Why now?
The online discourse regarding the geopolitical momentum toward the liberation of Iran has been plagued by propaganda. There have been many coordinated and targeted attempts to address this propaganda (by identifying posts, reacting in certain ways, etc.), with great success. An area of gap includes a lack of coordination in requesting Community Notes on X in response to high-profile posts that are simply propaganda or attempt to obstruct, delay, or reverse the geopolitical momentum toward freedom in Iran.
Key steps and help needed:
1- An organising body (e.g., a Media Support Telegram channel) identifies a high-profile post that hinders the freedom of Iran and/or involves propaganda.
2- The organising body identifies a post that disputes or counters the claim of the first post.
3- The organising body sends out a call to request a Community Note and informs the audience which post to tag.
4- The organising body and those eligible to be Community Notes moderators sign up for moderation and assist with drafting and publishing the Community Notes.
Supporting material:
When some high-profile posts are community-noted, media corporations use this in their narrative. One example of this was posts by Ilhan Omar (see attached screenshot).

items.title: Designing urban infrastructure for blind and visually impaired people
items.body:
Many people became blind on 18 /19th Dey. Designing urban infrastructure for blind and visually impaired people is about making environments safe, navigable, and independent-friendly. Here’s a brief, practical overview:


Tactile Guidance
•	Tactile paving (raised patterns) on sidewalks, crossings, and transit stations
•	Different textures signal direction, hazards, or stopping points


Audible Signals
•	Audio traffic lights that announce when it’s safe to cross
•	Public transport stops with voice announcements for arrivals and routes


Clear & Consistent Layout
•	Simple, predictable street layouts
•	Avoid unnecessary obstacles (random poles, clutter, uneven sidewalks)


High-Contrast Design
•	Use strong color contrast for partially sighted individuals
•	Mark edges of stairs, platforms, and curbs clearly


Safe Crossings
•	Longer crossing times at intersections
•	Detectable curb ramps aligned with crosswalks


Technology Integration
•	GPS-based navigation apps designed for blind users
•	Smart beacons that provide location-based audio guidance


Accessible Public Transport
•	Consistent stop locations
•	Staff training to assist visually impaired passengers


Hazard Reduction
•	Covered drains, smooth pathways, no sudden level changes
•	Proper maintenance to avoid unexpected dangers

items.title: AI in governance for equity and prosperity
items.body: In a country emerging from war or regime collapse, AI-driven governance can become a powerful foundation for restoring equity, trust, and economic recovery. By using data intelligently, governments can distribute aid more fairly, identify urgent needs in real time, and reduce corruption through transparent, traceable decision-making systems. For example, AI can optimize how humanitarian resources are allocated, ensuring that food, healthcare, and infrastructure investments reach the most affected populations quickly and efficiently  ￼. It can also help counter misinformation and social division—common in post-conflict environments—by identifying harmful narratives and promoting verified information, strengthening social cohesion  ￼. Beyond immediate recovery, AI enables inclusive governance by incorporating citizen input at scale, helping leaders make decisions that reflect the true needs of the population rather than centralized power. When implemented responsibly, with strong ethical frameworks like those advocated by global institutions, AI governance can accelerate the transition from instability to a more transparent, equitable, and prosperous society.
