A batch-based accelerator operating inside Iran that funds early-stage startups and helps them grow into scalable businesses.
What It Does
The accelerator selects cohorts of 10–15 startups 4 times a year, provides pre-seed funding in exchange for equity, and runs an intensive 3-month program. Teams go through structured training in product development, growth, and fundraising — then pitch to investors on Demo Day.
How It Works
Founders apply, get accepted into a batch, and move through the program together. The accelerator provides capital on day one, weekly sessions with mentors and operators, and hands-on support to hit milestones before Demo Day. After the program, companies join a permanent alumni network for follow-on fundraising and peer support.
Why Iran
Iran has one of the highest concentrations of engineering and technical graduates in the region, a population of 90 million with strong domestic demand, and a growing base of diaspora investors looking to back Iranian founders. What's missing is the infrastructure — a trusted, structured institution that takes early bets on founders and gives them the support to grow.
The Goal
Build the default institution for early-stage company-building in Iran — the place every ambitious founder applies to, and where the next generation of Iranian tech companies gets started.

items.title: Safeguarding Iranian Civil Society Ecosystem in a Post-Sanction Era
items.body:
The Context
As Iran moves toward potential reintegration with the international community, a surge of funding from international donors is anticipated. History — from the 2003 Bam Earthquake response to aid dynamics in Afghanistan and Sudan — warns that large financial inflows into fragile civil societies can trigger a "survival of the loudest" dynamic: well-networked, new born NGOS capture resources while grassroots communities with deeper local knowledge are systematically sidelined.
Iran's context adds layers of complexity. A powerful quasi-governmental foundation sector (bonyads), a legally constrained civil society, and an active diaspora with strong Western networks will all compete for the same resources. Without proactive safeguards, international funding risks entrenching existing power asymmetries rather than correcting them.
The Problem
The core risk is institutional access inequality — a structural gap between NGOs that can navigate donor bureaucracy and those that cannot. This manifests in three compounding ways:
•	The Communication Trap: Organizations fluent in English, grant-writing, and Western-style reporting secure disproportionate funding regardless of on-the-ground legitimacy.
•	Grassroots Erasure: Local organizations  are excluded not by merit, but by administrative burden.
•	Elite Capture Risk: Funding monopolies by a small cluster of bigger/ known NGOs inflate overhead, produce donor-pleasing but community-failing projects, and crowd out the very institutions development is meant to strengthen.
Proposed Framework: The Equitable Stewardship Body (ESB)
I propose an independently governed Equitable Stewardship Body with four core functions:
•	Equity Auditing: Assessing not just financial accountability, but knowledge equity — whether projects meaningfully integrate locally rooted partners, including those from minority regions.
•	Language Neutrality: Providing translation and technical support to decouple grant-writing proficiency from project merit.
•	The 60/40 Sub-Granting Rule: A minimum percentage of international funds must flow to or be co-led by provincial and neighborhood-level entities — with structural measures to prevent mainstream NGOs from creating nominal provincial subsidiaries to game the rule.
•	Transparency Ledger: A public, decentralized platform to track donor flows, prevent double-funding, and enable community accountability.
Critically, the ESB must include a built-in sunset clause — a mandatory governance review every five years — to prevent the body itself from becoming the new gatekeeper. Trustee selection models (rotating community jury, multi-stakeholder board, or blind peer-review consortium) are open questions for community deliberation. Additionally, any equity audit must integrate environmental sustainability criteria, given Iran's acute water scarcity and climate stress.
Interested in?
I welcome any collaboration from practitioners, researchers, community organizers, and diaspora voices — to contribute on any of the following:
•	Governance design for the ESB trustee model
•	Case documentation of the Bam 2003 aid response as a cautionary template
•	Mechanisms to incentivize institutionally strong NGOs to mentor grassroots groups rather than compete with them
•	Sustainability metrics — financial exit strategies and environmental impact criteria for equity audits
If you are interested in contributing, please comment below with your area of focus, or reach out directly to initiate a working group

items.title: Medical Tourism in Iran
items.body:
Iran has world-class doctors, modern hospitals, and medical costs a fraction of Europe or the Persian Gulf — but almost no one knows it yet. That's the opportunity.
The Idea
Build the infrastructure that turns Iran into a premier medical tourism destination. Not just a referral service — a full-stack operation that handles everything from the moment a patient decides to come to the moment they fly home: hospital partnerships, patient coordination, accommodation, translation, aftercare, and follow-up.
Why Iran
Iranian physicians are among the most rigorously trained in the region. Many completed fellowships in Europe or North America before returning. Specialties like cardiac surgery, orthopedics, ophthalmology, cosmetic surgery, dentistry, and fertility treatment are already at internationally competitive quality levels — at 20–40% of Western prices.
The country also has a 5,000-year hospitality culture, extraordinary food, and a diaspora of 5–8 million people who already have a reason to visit.
The Customer
Three clear segments:

Diaspora Iranians abroad who want quality care in a familiar language and culture
Regional patients from Iraq, Afghanistan, Central Asia, and the Persian Gulf seeking affordable high-quality treatment
International patients from Europe and beyond drawn by price, quality, and the novelty of a newly open country

What Gets Built
A coordinated platform connecting accredited hospitals and clinics with incoming patients — handling logistics end to end. Think of it as the operating layer that makes Iran legible and trustworthy to someone making a significant health decision from abroad.
The Bigger Picture
Medical tourism is a $100B+ global industry growing fast. Iran's combination of talent, price, and geography puts it in a position to capture a meaningful slice — if the right infrastructure exists to welcome patients and send them home healthy and satisfied.

items.title: GigaIran 2040: Youth-Driven Prosperity & Technological Renaissance
items.body:
Inspired by global models like Saudi Vision 2030, GigaIran 2040 is a bold national roadmap designed to transition Iran from an oil-dependent economy to a global green-tech powerhouse.
The centerpiece is a network of seven interconnected Gigafactories — massive, modern manufacturing and innovation hubs — each paired with dedicated Youth Skills Academies and Startup Incubators
Tesla-style Gigafactories have proven that mega-scale, vertically integrated facilities can create entire ecosystems of jobs, supply chains, and innovation.
Iran already possesses the raw ingredients: world-class solar resources, a strong engineering education system, an existing automotive and steel base, and strategic geography.
The Seven Strategic Gigafactories

GigaSolar, Largest solar/storage complex (25 GW target). Target: Yazd & Kerman.
2)GigaEv, Electric vehicles & Lithium-ion battery giants, Target Isfahan & Tabriz
3)GigaHydrogen, Green hydrogen via solar/wind electrolysis, Target south coast of Iran (Fars, Sistan Balouchestan, Boushehr)
4)GigaElectronics, Semiconductors, 5G/6G, and Data Center/SMT line Manufacturing, "Sister City to Shenzen" around Tehran province
5)GigaBioTech, Vaccines, biosimilars, and precision medicine,  multiple province
6)GigaCreative, Gaming, VFX, and digital content studios
7)GigaAgro-Tech, Vertical farming and food-processing automation

Youth-First Integration Programs
To ensure the workforce is ready, every Gigafactory sector specialized support systems:
GigaAcademy: Free 2-year STEM diplomas with guaranteed job placement.
GigaStartup Fund: A $5B sovereign fund providing 50% non-dilutive grants to youth-led startups.
GigaMentorship: Connecting the Iranian diaspora (Silicon Valley, Europe) with local talent.
GigaLife: On-site sports arenas, gyms, and music studios to promote work-life balance.
Strategic Roadmap
Phase 1 (2026–2030): Pilot launches in Yazd and Isfahan; 300,000 youths trained.
Phase 2 (2030–2035): Full network rollout; first EV and Green Hydrogen exports.
Phase 3 (2035–2040): Global leadership; Iran established as the "Green Tech Hub of the Middle East."

items.title: AI-Assisted Public Deliberation and Transparent Decision Infrastructure for Iran
items.body:
This is a civic-tech / public decision-making infrastructure idea that uses AI for deliberation support and blockchain for auditability and trust.
Iran needs more than regime change. It needs a trusted way for people to participate in shaping major public decisions.
This idea proposes a public decision-making platform that combines:

AI for moderating, summarizing, and comparing arguments
Blockchain for transparent, tamper-evident records
Public participation for reviewing, debating, and influencing decisions

Why Iran
One of the biggest problems in any transition is trust.
People may disagree on political figures, systems, and ideologies, but they also do not trust closed-door decisions, unclear deals, or vague promises about what comes next.
Iran may soon face difficult questions such as:

what principles should guide a temporary government
what powers should or should not be given during transition
which constitutional options should be considered
how minority concerns should be preserved
how public input should be documented and respected

Right now, public debate is fragmented, emotional, and easy to distort.
This proposal is meant to create a more structured and transparent process.
What it looks like
A public platform where proposals, political principles, and policy options can be discussed in a structured way.
It would allow:

individuals or groups to submit proposals
arguments for and against each proposal to be collected
AI to summarize both sides in plain language
AI to detect overlap, contradiction, repeated concerns, and missing points
participants to compare options without reading thousands of scattered comments
proposal history, edits, reasoning, and voting records to be preserved transparently

Why this works
1. AI helps with scale
AI can:

summarize large volumes of comments
group similar arguments together
show the strongest points from each side
detect contradictions between proposals
explain complex debates in simpler language

AI should not make the final decision.
Its role is to act as a moderator, analyst, explainer, and contradiction detector.
2. Blockchain helps with trust
Blockchain can provide:

tamper-evident records of proposals and revisions
transparent audit trails for votes and decisions
verifiable timestamps
protection against silent edits or hidden manipulation
stronger legitimacy for the process

Not everything should be on-chain. Sensitive identity and personal data should remain protected off-chain, while hashes, proofs, timestamps, and final records can be stored on-chain.
Example use case
Imagine two or more groups debating a major issue such as:

tax policy
subsidy reform
privatization
education policy
public health rules
transitional constitutional principles

Instead of the debate becoming a chaotic fight, the platform would structure it:

a proposal is submitted
arguments for and against are collected
AI summarizes both sides
contradictions with previous principles or decisions are flagged
public response and voting are recorded
final reasoning and outcome are preserved transparently

This creates a visible reasoning chain, not just a final result.
Why this could be valuable
This could help Iran build a transition process that is:

more transparent
more reviewable
less dependent on personalities alone
more open to public reasoning
harder to manipulate silently

It also gives minority viewpoints a place in the record, which matters because sometimes ignored concerns later become major national issues.
Main risks
This idea is only useful if it is designed carefully.
Main risks include:

biased AI summaries
fake participation or bot manipulation
weak identity verification
overcomplicating the system
using blockchain where a normal database would be enough
making people think AI is deciding instead of people

So the system should stay practical and restrained.
Use AI where scale and clarity are needed.
Use blockchain where auditability really matters.
Suggested first pilot
This should not begin as a full national governance system.
A realistic pilot could start with one public issue:

allow a few competing proposals
collect structured comments
use AI to summarize and compare
record proposal history and voting transparently
test whether users find the process clearer and more trustworthy

Start small. Prove value first.
Help needed
Looking for people with experience in:

civic tech
governance design
digital identity
cryptography and privacy
blockchain systems
AI moderation and summarization
law and constitutional thinking
product design for public participation

Main question
Can Iran build a public decision process that is more transparent, more reviewable, and more participatory than both closed political bargaining and chaotic online debate?
This idea is one possible direction.

items.title: The Museum of Persian Civilization
items.body:
English:
Iran's next great cultural landmark should be a Museum of Persian Civilization — a sweeping architectural tribute modeled after the grandeur of Persepolis at its height, before centuries of conquest and ruin reduced it to the magnificent fragments we know today. Rising from the landscape as Persepolis once did, with its forest of towering columns, ornate bas-reliefs, and monumental gateways, the museum would not merely house Persian history — it would be Persian history, rendered in stone and light. Visitors would walk corridors echoing the Apadana Palace, and feel, for the first time, what it meant to stand at the center of the ancient world's most powerful empire. It would serve as a diplomatic magnet for the repatriation of Persian artifacts currently scattered across Western institutions, reclaiming not just objects but sovereignty over Iran's own narrative. Beyond its cultural mission, the museum would be a transformative economic engine, drawing millions of international visitors annually.
Persian:
نماد فرهنگی بزرگ بعدی ایران باید «موزه‌ی تمدن ایران» باشد؛ ادای احترامی معمارانه و باشکوه که از عظمت تخت‌جمشید در دوران اوجش الگوبرداری شده است، پیش از آنکه سده‌ها فتح و ویرانی، آن را به بقایای شکوهمندی که امروز می‌شناسیم تقلیل دهد. این موزه که همچون تخت‌جمشیدِ کهن از دلِ منظره سر برمی‌آورد، با جنگلی از ستون‌های سر به فلک کشیده، نقش‌برجسته‌های پرنقش‌ونگار و دروازه‌های عظیم، تنها پناهگاهی برای تاریخ ایران نخواهد بود؛ بلکه خودِ تاریخ ایران خواهد بود که در کالبد سنگ و نور تجسم یافته است. بازدیدکنندگان در راهروهایی قدم خواهند زد که یادآور کاخ آپاداناست و برای نخستین بار حس خواهند کرد که ایستادن در مرکز قدرتمندترین امپراتوری جهان باستان چه معنایی داشته است. این بنا همچون آهنربایی دیپلماتیک برای بازگرداندن آثار باستانی ایران که اکنون در نهادهای غربی پراکنده‌اند عمل خواهد کرد و نه تنها اشیاء، بلکه حاکمیت بر روایتِ تاریخیِ خودِ ایران را باز پس خواهد گرفت. فراتر از مأموریت فرهنگی، این موزه یک موتور اقتصادیِ تحول‌آفرین خواهد بود که سالانه میلیون‌ها بازدیدکننده‌ی بین‌المللی را به سوی خود جذب می‌کند.

items.title: برای آنان که صدایی ندارند  - دفاع از حقوق حیوانات
items.body:
در ایرانِ پس از آزادی و استقرار دموکراسی، ارتقای فرهنگ عمومی و نهادینه‌سازی ارزش‌های انسانی از جمله احترام به حیات همه موجودات زنده، از اولویت‌های اساسی خواهد بود. حمایت از حیوانات بی‌سرپرست و به رسمیت شناختن حقوق آن‌ها، نشانه‌ای از بلوغ اخلاقی جامعه است. حیوانات نیز موجوداتی دارای احساس و حق زیستن هستند و باید در برابر خشونت، آزار و بی‌توجهی مورد حمایت قانونی قرار گیرند. در ایران آینده، لازم است قوانین مشخص و محکمی برای منع حیوان‌آزاری، حمایت از حیوانات بی‌سرپرست، و مسئولیت‌پذیری صاحبان حیوانات تدوین و اجرا شود تا کرامت حیات به یک اصل بنیادین تبدیل گردد.
هدف من این است که با ترکیبی از آموزش، قانون‌گذاری و مشارکت مردمی، فرهنگ صحیح رفتار با حیوانات را در جامعه تقویت کنم. این مسیر می‌تواند شامل آموزش در مدارس، کمپین‌های آگاهی‌رسانی، برنامه‌های عقیم‌سازی و واکسیناسیون (TNR)، توسعه پناهگاه‌های استاندارد، و ایجاد خطوط گزارش‌دهی برای موارد حیوان‌آزاری باشد. همچنین حمایت از سازمان‌های مردم‌نهاد و داوطلبان، و همکاری با شهرداری‌ها برای مدیریت انسانی حیوانات شهری ضروری است. ایرانِ آزاد می‌تواند الگویی باشد از همزیستی مسئولانه انسان و حیوان، جایی که حقوق حیوانات به رسمیت شناخته شده و مهربانی بخشی از هویت ملی ما باشد.

items.title: Urgent Open Letter to Trump & Netanyahu, Protect Iranian Civilians from Blackout
items.body:
Urgent Open Letter to President Trump and Prime Minister Netanyahu
نامه سرگشاده فوری به رئیس‌جمهور ترامپ و نخست‌وزیر نتانیاهو
President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu,
The Iranian people are being held hostage by the terrorist regime, which has imposed a total internet blackout to conceal its crimes and is eagerly preparing scorched-earth repression in the darkness.
We strongly urge you to immediately withdraw the threat of striking Iran’s power plants and electricity infrastructure as part of the 48-hour ultimatum. Such an attack would plunge millions of innocent civilians into complete darkness exactly what the IRGC wants to enable mass suppression under blackout conditions.
Instead, we respectfully call for smart and targeted maximum pressure that protects the Iranian people and accelerates a peaceful democratic transition:
-Undertake effective and systematic action with regard to state-controlled media mechanisms, particularly the national broadcasting system, within legal frameworks and internationally recognized standards, with the aim of ending information monopolies and enhancing transparency.


Pursue firm and continuous accountability of senior officials through domestic and international legal mechanisms, with an emphasis on the rule of law and the principle of no impunity.


Provide practical, tangible, and reliable support to citizens to ensure their ability to exercise fundamental rights, including peaceful assembly and civic participation, in accordance with legal frameworks and international obligations.


Enforce complete sanctions on all Iranian oil exports, especially to China


Immediately expand Starlink on a massive scale to break the information blackout


Formally recognize Reza Pahlavi and the democratic opposition as the legitimate representatives of the Iranian people’s will


No harm to civilian infrastructure is needed. This intelligent pressure will force the regime’s formal surrender without punishing the Iranian people saving countless lives and opening the path to real freedom.
The Iranian diaspora stands with you for a secular Iran.

نسخه فارسی نامه (برای پست در شبکه‌های ایرانی):
رئیس‌جمهور دونالد ترامپ و نخست‌وزیر بنیامین نتانیاهو،
مردم ایران توسط رژیم تروریست گروگان گرفته شده‌اند. این رژیم اینترنت را کامل قطع کرده تا جنایاتش را پنهان کند و برای سرکوب در تاریکی کامل آماده می‌شود.
ما به شدت درخواست می‌کنیم "تهدید حمله به نیروگاه‌ها و زیرساخت برق ایران" را فوراً لغو کنید. چنین حمله‌ای میلیون‌ها غیرنظامی را در تاریکی کامل فرو می‌برد، دقیقاً همان چیزی که سپاه پاسداران می‌خواهد تا سرکوب گسترده را در خاموشی کامل انجام دهد.
به جای آن، از فشار هوشمند و هدفمند استفاده کنید که مردم ایران را حفظ کند و گذار دموکراتیک مسالمت‌آمیز را سرعت ببخشد:


اقدام مؤثر و نظام‌مند در قبال سازوکارهای رسانه‌ای تحت کنترل دولت، به‌ویژه نهاد پخش صدا و سیمای جمهوری اسلامی، در چارچوب ابزارهای قانونی و استانداردهای بین‌المللی، با هدف پایان دادن به انحصار اطلاع‌رسانی و ارتقای شفافیت.


برخورد قاطع و مستمر پاسخگویی مقامات ارشد از طریق سازوکارهای حقوقی داخلی و بین‌المللی، با تأکید بر حاکمیت قانون و اصل عدم مصونیت.


فراهم‌سازی حمایت‌های عملی، ملموس و قابل اتکا برای شهروندان، به‌منظور تضمین امکان بهره‌مندی از حقوق بنیادین از جمله تجمعات مسالمت‌آمیز و مشارکت مدنی، در چارچوب قوانین و تعهدات بین‌المللی


تحریم کامل صادرات نفت ایران (به‌ویژه به چین)


گسترش فوری و گسترده استارلینک برای شکستن خاموشی اطلاعاتی مردم ایران


به‌رسمیت شناختن شاهزاده رضا پهلوی و اپوزیسیون دموکراتیک به عنوان نماینده مشروع مردم ایران


هیچ آسیبی به زیرساخت‌های غیرنظامی لازم نیست. این فشار هوشمند رژیم را وادار به تسلیم رسمی می‌کند بدون اینکه مردم ایران مجازات شوند.

items.body:
Air Is Ours Live, Create, Move On.
In Tehran, space is limited.
This project offers a light, flexible alternative.
Inflatable structures made from recycled plastic.
Easy to build. Easy to remove.
No permanent foundation.
Each unit has one function:
sleep, work, gather.
Together, they form a temporary system.
Inspired by raumlaborberlin, Hans-Walter Müller, and Plastique Fantastique,
it can house youth and artists for up to a year.
A real place to live, create, and connect.
A bridge to their next future home.
The structure appears when needed.
It disappears without trace.
Funding comes from art, projections, small events, and temporary advertisements.
The system grows from its own activity.
Users build it themselves.
They shape the space.
What remains is not the object,
but the experience,
the skills,
the network,
the next step.

items.title: Planting the Future: Remote Learning Centers for Underserved Children
items.body:
Abstract
This idea proposes building low-cost, remotely managed learning centers for children in underserved regions of Iran.
Many areas lack schools, teachers, and access to devices, making education difficult or impossible.
By using shared devices, internet access, and centralized online teaching, these centers reduce cost while scaling education without relying on local teachers.
The facilities can be operated and monitored remotely, enabling efficient deployment even in hard-to-reach areas.
Why it matters
Education is a critical driver of economic recovery and long-term national stability.
Without access to education, underserved regions face workforce shortages, reduced productivity, and widening inequality.
Investing in accessible education infrastructure ensures that all regions can develop skilled human capital.
This enables local communities to participate in rebuilding their economies and reduces long-term dependency on central resources.
Approach
Each learning center is a simple, low-cost facility equipped with shared devices, internet access, and a large screen for group learning.
The centers are designed to operate with minimal or no on-site staff, using remote monitoring and access control systems.
Education is delivered primarily through AI-based learning systems, supported by centralized teachers who connect with students online on a regular basis (e.g., once or twice per month).
Students follow a fixed timetable, allowing efficient scheduling and remote management of the facility.
Additionally, students periodically interact with peers from other cities through online sessions, helping build national awareness and communication skills.

items.title: طرح آزادسازی سرمایه‌های ملی منجمد شده در اماکن مذهبی
items.body:
بیان مسئله (Problem Statement)
پس از فروپاشی نظام‌های ایدئولوژیک، مدیریت اماکن مذهبی که دهه‌ها از بودجه عمومی تغذیه کرده‌اند، یکی از چالش‌های اصلی است. از سویی، تخریب این اماکن منجربه هدررفت سرمایه ملی و ایجاد تنش‌های اجتماعی عمیق (و احتمال شکل‌گیری اپوزیسیون مذهبی جدید علیه سکولاریسم در دهه‌های آینده) می‌شود. از سوی دیگر، ادامه روند فعلی و تزریق بودجه دولتی به این مراکز با اصول سکولاریسم در تضاد است.
پرسش اصلی: چگونه می‌توان سرمایه‌های ملی صرف شده را به خزانه بازگرداند؟

راهکار پیشنهادی (The Solution)
این طرح در ۴ قدم اجرایی تدوین شده است:
۱. ملی‌سازی و انتقال مالکیت
تمام اماکن مذهبی که در طول ۴۷ سال گذشته به هر نحوی (مستقیم یا غیرمستقیم) بودجه دولتی دریافت کرده‌اند، مصادره شده و در مالکیت حقوقی دولت جدید قرار می‌گیرند.
۲. قیمت‌گذاری مبتنی بر بازده سرمایه (Audit)
قیمت پایه این اماکن بر اساس فرمول زیر محاسبه می‌شود:
فرمول: (مجموع بودجه‌های دریافتی سالانه) + (نرخ تورم تجمیعی) + (ارزش افزوده ناشی از سرمایه‌گذاری فرضی آن پول در زیرساخت‌های ملی).
هدف این است که قیمت به قدری واقعی و بالا باشد که تمام هزینه‌هایی که ملت برای آن مکان پرداخته‌اند، بازپس گرفته شود.
به عنوان مثلا یک مکان مذهبی 100 مترمربعی در یک شهر کوچک ممکن است 100میلیون دلار ارزش گذاری شود. یا مثلا یک مکان مذهبی معروف در تجریش ممکن است 20میلیارد دلار ارزش گذاری شود.
۳. برگزاری مزایده عمومی (Public Auction)
تک‌تک این اماکن به مزایده گذاشته می‌شوند. هر شخص، گروه یا نهاد مذهبی که توانایی پرداخت قیمت کارشناسی شده را داشته باشد، می‌تواند مالکیت آن را بر عهده گرفته و هزینه‌های نگهداری آن را شخصاً تامین کند.
وجوه حاصل از این مزایده‌ها مستقیماً به پروژه‌های زیرساختی ملی (آموزش، بهداشت, صنعت, تکنولوژی و...) به نفع مردم واریز می‌شود.
۴. تغییر کاربری دموکراتیک (Public Referendum)
در صورتی که ملکی در مزایده به فروش نرسد (به دلیل نبود خریدار یا عدم توانایی مالی گروه‌های مذهبی در پرداخت قیمت واقعی)، سرنوشت آن ملک با رای‌گیری عمومی مشخص می‌شود. مردم تصمیم می‌گیرند که ملک به چه چیزی تغییر کاربری دهد.

ملاحظات و محدودیت‌ها (Considerations)
حاکمیت قانون: مالکیت شخصی یا گروهی پس از برنده شدن در مزایده، به معنای مصونیت از قانون نیست. تمام فعالیت‌های مذهبی در این اماکن باید ذیل قوانین جدید سکولار (در زمینه‌های آلودگی صوتی، ترافیک و محدودیت‌های مدنی) انجام شود.
قطع وابستگی: با اجرای این طرح، دولت هیچ‌گونه مسئولیتی در قبال نگهداری، بازسازی یا تامین حقوق کارکنان این اماکن نخواهد داشت.

items.title: Construction of a solar power plant in the Lut and dashte-kavir Desert
items.body:
Construction of Large-Scale Solar Power Plants in the Lut and Dasht-e Kavir Deserts
Idea:
Develop large-scale solar power plants in Iran’s Lut Desert and Dasht-e Kavir Desert to generate clean electricity at national scale, strengthen energy security, support industry, and create a foundation for future electricity exports and green industrial growth.
Why Iran:
• Iran has vast desert land with very high solar irradiation
• The Lut and Dasht-e Kavir regions offer large, sparsely populated areas suitable for utility-scale solar development
• Iran has growing electricity demand and rising pressure on gas-fired generation
• Solar can reduce fuel consumption, lower grid stress, and diversify the national energy mix
What it looks like:
• Large utility-scale solar farms in high-irradiation desert zones
• Grid connection through new transmission corridors and substations
• Phased development starting with priority sites closest to existing grid infrastructure
• Potential integration with battery storage, desalination, hydrogen production, or industrial zones over time
Why this works:
• Iran has the natural conditions needed for world-class solar generation
• Desert land availability reduces land-use conflict with cities and agriculture
• Solar plants can be built in phases, making rollout more practical and financeable
• The project supports both domestic electricity needs and long-term industrial strategy
Impact:
• More clean electricity generation
• Reduced dependence on fossil-fuel-based power during peak demand
• Lower pressure on domestic gas consumption
• Job creation in engineering, construction, operations, and maintenance
• Stronger energy resilience in remote and high-growth regions
• Foundation for future energy-intensive industries powered by solar electricity
Approach:
define priority solar development zones in the Lut and Dasht-e Kavir deserts based on irradiation, land suitability, environmental constraints, and distance to transmission infrastructure.
launch a first phase of utility-scale pilot projects near viable grid-connection points to prove technical and financial performance.
expand transmission capacity, substations, and smart-grid systems to carry desert-generated electricity to demand centers.
develop a financing and regulatory framework that enables public investment, private participation, and long-term power-purchase certainty.
integrate complementary systems such as battery storage, hybrid renewable clusters, industrial loads, and water solutions where economically justified.
build local technical capacity for installation, maintenance, component supply, and desert-environment operations.
A realistic rollout would begin with site studies and pilot projects in the first 12–18 months, followed by multi-phase scaling over 3–7 years depending on transmission buildout, financing, and regulatory support.
Help Needed:
Energy planners, solar engineers, transmission and grid specialists, desert-environment infrastructure experts, environmental assessment teams, financing partners, legal and regulatory advisors, land and permitting authorities, EPC contractors, equipment suppliers, storage specialists, and public-sector energy institutions. Funding would be needed for feasibility studies, grid interconnection, project development, environmental review, pilot construction, and long-term scaling.

items.title: Develop Street-Running Tram / Light Rail in Tehran and Other Iranian Cities Instead of Relying Mainly on Buses
items.body:
Idea:
Develop street-running tram and light rail systems in Tehran and other major Iranian cities to provide cleaner, higher-capacity, and more reliable urban transport on the busiest corridors, while integrating with existing metro, BRT, and bus networks. In practice, this works best as a replacement for buses on selected high-demand trunk corridors, not as a total replacement for buses everywhere. Tehran already has a strong metro and BRT base, and Iran already has multiple cities with urban rail systems, which makes this a realistic next step rather than a completely new model.
Why Iran:
• Iran already has urban rail operating beyond Tehran, including in Mashhad, Shiraz, Isfahan, Tabriz, and Karaj, so the country has a wider rail base that can support expansion into more surface-rail formats.
• Tehran has studied LRT lines, which shows that street-running rail is already part of the policy conversation.
• Tehran also continues to build domestic rolling-stock capability, including metro train production with high domestic content, which could support broader urban rail development.
• Cleaner urban transport matters because transport emissions and air quality have long been a major policy issue in Tehran.
What it looks like:
• Modern street-running tram or light rail lines on major city corridors in Tehran and other large cities
• Dedicated or semi-dedicated lanes, signal priority, high-quality stops, and safer pedestrian access
• Strong interchange with metro stations, BRT corridors, intercity terminals, and dense commercial districts
• Electric vehicles with quieter service and lower local emissions than conventional diesel bus operations
• Tehran as the first and largest pilot, followed by corridor-based rollout in cities such as Mashhad, Shiraz, Isfahan, Tabriz, and Karaj where rail ecosystems already exist
Why this works:
• Tehran is already a rail-and-BRT city, so a street-running tram layer can complement the metro instead of competing with it.
• Iran is not starting from zero: several major cities already operate metro systems, and Tehran has already explored LRT.
• The strongest use case is on corridors where ordinary bus service is heavily used and where more permanence, smoother rides, and higher-capacity electric service would improve reliability and urban quality. That is especially relevant in Tehran, where BRT already functions as a backbone and surface public transport demand is clearly large.
• At the same time, UITP notes that BRT remains a scalable and cost-effective mode, so the practical model is not “rail everywhere,” but “rail for the busiest trunks, buses for feeder and coverage service.”
Impact:
• Higher-capacity and more reliable transit on the busiest urban corridors
• Lower local emissions and less noise from surface public transport
• Better connections between neighborhoods, metro stations, and major activity centers
• Improved street design through upgraded sidewalks, crossings, stops, and public-space redesign
• Reduced dependence on diesel bus fleets on the corridors where ridership is strongest
• A stronger long-term urban transport model for Tehran and other growing Iranian cities with existing or emerging rail systems
Approach:
identify the highest-demand corridors in Tehran first, then in other major cities, where street-running rail would outperform standard bus service in capacity, comfort, and long-term corridor quality.
start with corridor studies that assess ridership, road width, station spacing, traffic impacts, utility relocation, pedestrian access, and integration with existing metro and BRT lines.
launch a first phase in Tehran as the national demonstration project, using dedicated or mostly dedicated lanes, modern platforms, traffic-signal priority, and integrated fares. Tehran is the logical first pilot because it already has the country’s largest metro and BRT base and has studied LRT.
expand to other suitable cities such as Mashhad, Shiraz, Isfahan, Tabriz, and Karaj, especially where existing metro systems can connect with new surface rail corridors.
keep buses in the network as feeder, neighborhood, and lower-density services rather than trying to eliminate them completely, since BRT and bus systems remain useful and more flexible on many corridors.
use domestic rail manufacturing and engineering capacity where possible for rolling stock, maintenance, and systems supply.
A realistic rollout would begin with 12–18 months of corridor selection, feasibility studies, and pilot design, followed by 2–5 years for first-line delivery in Tehran and then phased expansion to other cities over the following years, depending on funding, street redesign needs, and utility relocation complexity.
Help Needed:
Urban rail planners, tram and LRT engineers, transport modelers, city street-design teams, traffic-signal specialists, accessibility experts, environmental and air-quality specialists, rolling-stock manufacturers, fare-integration and ticketing teams, legal and regulatory advisors, municipal transit agencies, financing partners, and pilot-city governments. Funding would be needed for corridor studies, civil works, stations, depots, utility relocation, rolling stock, signaling, and network integration.

items.title: A Digital-Ready State for a New Iran
items.body:
Build governance for the age of information and AI — safely, transparently, and step by step.

TL;DR:
A new Iran should not copy state structures designed for the age of paper, distance, and slow communication. Whatever constitutional form Iran chooses, it should build a government that is digital-ready by design, hybrid in operation, and human in accountability.
The goal is not to make everything online immediately.
The goal is to build institutions so that digitalization can happen safely, gradually, and reversibly as trust, infrastructure, and public readiness grow.

1. Core Idea
Iran should build a state that combines the strengths of both systems:

Digital systems for speed, scale, transparency, and auditability
Human institutions for judgment, legitimacy, appeals, and accountability
Physical/offline channels for resilience, inclusion, and fallback

In other words:

Digital by design. Hybrid in operation. Human in accountability.


2. Constitutional Form Does Not Change the Need
This proposal is neutral on whether Iran becomes a monarchy or a republic.
The question here is not who holds symbolic or executive power.
The question is how the state itself works:

How records are kept
How services are delivered
How corruption is reduced
How citizens verify decisions
How technology strengthens, rather than weakens, legitimacy

A modern Iran needs modern state capacity under any constitutional model.

3. Design Principles
1. Resilience over hype
No critical service should depend on one app, one vendor, one ministry, or one server.
2. Digitize the safest things first
Start with services that are high-value and low-risk. Move slowly toward sensitive areas.
3. Keep a human appeals path
Any significant state decision must be reviewable by a human.
4. Preserve offline access
During transition, citizens must still be able to use physical channels.
5. Open standards and auditability
Core public systems should use open standards, clear logs, and independent review.
6. Privacy by design
The state should only collect what it truly needs, and sensitive systems should be separated.
7. Reversible adoption
If a digital system fails, is abused, or loses trust, the state must be able to roll back safely.

4. Build the State So It Can Be Digitized Later
The smartest move is not to digitize everything immediately.
It is to make every new law, regulation, and service easy to digitize later.
That means every new public process should have:

a clear legal definition
explicit decision rules
a machine-readable form/schema
an audit log requirement
a privacy and data-minimization rule
a human review and appeals process
an offline/manual fallback

This avoids a common problem: countries try to digitize broken, vague, paper-era processes and end up automating confusion.
Iran should do the opposite:

Standardize first. Digitize second. Scale third.


5. What to Digitize First, Next, and Last



Priority
Examples
Why




First
Civil records, company registration, tax filing, permit tracking, public procurement, land record access, court/case status
High public value, lower political risk, major anti-corruption gains


Next
Benefits administration, licensing workflows, municipal services, public consultation, participatory budgeting
Useful, but needs stronger oversight and appeals


Last
National online voting, constitutional referenda, fully automated high-stakes decisions
Requires the highest trust, security, legitimacy, and public confidence



The sequencing matters.
A credible proposal should begin with state capacity and transparency, not with the most controversial use of technology.

6. The Role of AI
AI can give Iran a real advantage — but only if used carefully.
Good early uses of AI

document processing
translation and multilingual citizen support
fraud and anomaly detection
case triage and routing
summarizing laws and procedures for citizens
helping civil servants process routine requests faster
detecting procurement irregularities and corruption patterns
policy modeling and scenario analysis

Red lines

no black-box criminal sentencing
no secret models in core state functions
no unappealable denial of rights or benefits
no fully automated decisions in high-stakes constitutional matters
no AI replacing legal accountability

The right model is:

AI as assistant, auditor, and accelerator — not sovereign decision-maker.


7. Elections and Political Participation
Digital democracy should be introduced in layers.
Layer 1 — Transparency
Start with:

digital voter rolls
public result reporting
audit trails
open publication of election procedures
chain-of-custody transparency

Layer 2 — Civic participation
Introduce:

e-petitions
public consultations
participatory budgeting
municipal issue polling
structured public feedback on draft laws

Layer 3 — Local pilots
Run limited pilots for digital voting or delegated participation at the municipal level, with:

paper backup
independent audits
open-source review
clear rollback plans

Layer 4 — National adoption
Only after repeated successful pilots should Iran consider wider digital voting systems, and even then only with:

end-to-end verifiability
strong privacy protections
independent certification
paper audit capability where needed
multi-party oversight

This is the strongest and most defensible position:

Do not start with national online voting. Earn trust through lower-risk systems first.


8. A Hybrid Democracy Model
Iran does not need to choose between:

a purely old-style representative system, or
pure direct digital democracy

A stronger model is hybrid:

representatives remain necessary for continuity and negotiation
citizens gain direct tools gradually
local issues can be more participatory than national ones
delegation can be flexible and issue-specific
constitutional rights remain protected from majoritarian abuse

This allows modern participation without destabilizing the entire state.

9. Technical Architecture Principles
A digital-ready state should be built on a few simple technical foundations:
Identity and credentials
Secure digital identity for citizens, with strong legal protections and multiple ways to authenticate.
Interoperable records
Government databases should use shared standards and APIs, not isolated silos.
Auditability
Every important action in a public workflow should leave a verifiable trace.
Separation of sensitive systems
Identity, health, taxation, policing, and voting should not collapse into one giant surveillance database.
Offline-first resilience
Essential systems should continue functioning during outages, cyberattacks, or connectivity problems.
No vendor lock-in
Core state systems should be replaceable and built on open standards.

10. Anti-Corruption by Design
One of the biggest advantages of digital governance is not convenience.
It is reducing discretionary corruption.
Everywhere the state relies on:

unclear rules
hidden queues
discretionary signatures
fragmented records
untraceable exceptions

corruption grows.
A digital-ready state can reduce this by making processes:

rule-based
time-stamped
auditable
publicly measurable
harder to manipulate in secret

This does not eliminate corruption by itself.
But it makes corruption more detectable, more expensive, and less scalable.

11. Roadmap
Phase 1 — Foundations

digital rights and data protection law
standards for digital identity and credentials
interoperability rules for government systems
public procurement transparency rules
cybersecurity and disaster recovery standards

Phase 2 — Service Delivery

digitize the most common public services
create case tracking and status transparency
reduce paperwork and in-person bottlenecks
retrain civil servants as supervisors, investigators, and case managers

Phase 3 — Oversight and Transparency

publish budgets, procurement, and service performance
deploy anomaly detection for waste and fraud
establish independent technical audit bodies

Phase 4 — Civic Participation

launch e-petitions and consultations
test participatory budgeting locally
pilot delegated/local digital participation

Phase 5 — High-Trust Democratic Tools

pilot verifiable digital voting carefully
expand only if security, legitimacy, and trust are clearly proven


12. Non-Negotiable Rights
Any digital governance model for Iran should guarantee:

the right to privacy
the right to a human appeal
the right to non-digital access during transition
the right to transparency in public algorithms
the right to independent verification of public counts and election processes
the right not to be subject to hidden automated state power


13. Why This Matters for Iran
Iran has a rare chance to leapfrog.
Just as some countries skipped landlines and went straight to mobile, Iran can avoid rebuilding a paper-heavy, slow, opaque state and instead build one that is:

faster
cleaner
more auditable
more inclusive of the diaspora
less vulnerable to petty corruption
more competitive in an AI-driven world

The opportunity is not just administrative. It is strategic.
A country that builds modern state capacity from the start will have an edge in:

governance
trust
talent retention
investment
public service delivery
national resilience


Conclusion
The goal is not to create a “techno-state.”
The goal is to create a state that is harder to corrupt, easier to audit, faster to use, and better suited to the age of networks and AI.
Iran should not inherit the administrative assumptions of the telegraph era.
It should build institutions for the information era:

Digital by design. Hybrid in operation. Human in accountability.


This should be a living document. Fork it, criticize it, improve it, and adapt it to the constitutional structure Iran ultimately chooses.

items.title: AI-Driven Hardware Manufacturing Hub
items.body:
Iran has the potential to establish itself as a regional center for AI-driven hardware manufacturing by enabling large-scale imports of advanced hardware systems and tooling through strategic partnerships with global technology companies, such as ASML. The country could develop specialized industrial zones where international firms collaborate with local businesses. The primary focus could initially be on the assembly, integration, and adaptation of imported high-tech equipment, rather than full-scale semiconductor production. This approach may facilitate rapid entry into the global value chain while minimizing capital risk.
Moreover, Iran's engineering workforce, particularly in electronics and embedded systems, could be utilized to improve and integrate these hardware systems with AI, resulting in solutions applicable across healthcare, manufacturing, logistics, and service sectors. By merging imported hardware with domestically developed AI capabilities, Iran may progressively advance from assembly to innovation, fostering a sustainable ecosystem of AI-enabled devices and smart industrial systems that could contribute to long-term technological and economic growth.

items.title: Iran Medical Imaging AI Ecosystem (IMIAIE)
items.body:
I think a future Iran should build an ecosystem for AI in medical imaging (or AI in Medicine as more general term).
The goal is not to create one giant company or one tool that does everything. The better idea is to create the right space for many startups and teams to work on different real healthcare problems.
For example, one startup could work on AI for faster stroke detection in brain scans. Another could focus on eye screening for diabetic patients. Another could help with cancer imaging, mammography, chest X-rays, or radiology workflow.
This is important because medical imaging is one of the most practical areas for AI. If used correctly, it can help doctors find urgent cases faster, improve screening, reduce delays, and bring better healthcare to more people.
This ecosystem should connect:

hospitals
doctors
engineers
universities
startups

It should also make it easier to test ideas safely in real clinical settings, so good projects do not stay only as research papers and can become real tools that help patients.
In short, this idea is about building a strong foundation so that many useful medical imaging startups can grow in Iran in the future.

items.title: Iran Wildfire Analyst — سیستم پیشگیری و اخطار آتش سوزی ها در طبیعت
items.body:
Iran Wildfire Analyst — AI-Powered Early Warning System for Iran's Forests and Wildlands
Abstract
Iran loses thousands of hectares of forest and rangeland to wildfires every year — in provinces like Fars, Kohgiluyeh, Khuzestan, and the Zagros highlands. Most fires are detected too late, when containment is already difficult and ecological damage is done.
Iran Wildfire Analyst is an open-source, AI-powered wildfire detection and alerting system that turns raw satellite data into actionable intelligence in near real-time. It ingests NASA FIRMS satellite fire detections, enriches them with weather, vegetation, and air-quality data, and uses an LLM-assisted scoring engine to prioritize genuine threats — then pushes alerts to responders.
A working MVP already exists in two repositories:

iran-wildfire-analyst — The core detection pipeline (satellite ingest → enrichment → scoring → alerting)
wildfire-mcp-server — An MCP server interface for querying wildfire data through AI assistants

Why It's Interesting

Iran's forests are irreplaceable. The Zagros oak forests and Hyrcanian forests (a UNESCO World Heritage site) took thousands of years to grow. Every fire season they shrink further. Early detection is the single highest-leverage intervention.
The technology is accessible now. NASA's satellite fire data is free. Weather and land-cover APIs are free. LLMs can run affordably. What has been missing is someone stitching these together for Iran specifically — this project does exactly that.
It scales from MVP to national platform. The current version runs on free APIs and a single machine. With modest investment it can integrate physical IoT sensors, drone feeds, and real-time ground-truth — becoming a comprehensive nature-protection platform, not just for fire but for deforestation, drought, and biodiversity monitoring.
It can save lives and livelihoods. Wildfires threaten rural communities, livestock, and the firefighters who battle them with limited resources. Faster alerts mean faster response, smaller fires, and fewer casualties.

Approach
Phase 1 — Strengthen the MVP (Now)

Improve satellite detection accuracy with additional data sources (Landsat, Sentinel-2)
Expand alerting beyond Telegram — a simple web dashboard and mobile notifications
Add historical fire analysis to identify high-risk zones before fire season

Phase 2 — Ground-Truth Integration

Partner with forestry departments to deploy low-cost IoT sensors (temperature, humidity, smoke) in high-risk areas
Combine satellite detections with sensor readings for higher confidence and faster response
Build a public-facing map and reporting interface

Phase 3 — National Nature Protection Platform

Extend beyond fire to deforestation tracking, drought monitoring, and air quality
Provide seasonal risk forecasts using historical data and climate models
API access for fire departments, provincial governments, and environmental NGOs

Help Needed

Backend / Data Engineers — to scale the pipeline and integrate new data sources
Mobile / Frontend Developers — to build a responder app and public dashboard
Environmental / Forestry Experts — domain knowledge on Iran's fire-prone regions, vegetation types, and response workflows
IoT / Hardware Engineers — for sensor integration in Phase 2
Funding & Partnerships — cloud infrastructure, sensor hardware, and connections to Iran's Department of Environment or provincial forestry offices

Supporting Material

Live repositories:

iran-wildfire-analyst — full pipeline with DAG-based agent orchestration, multi-source data fusion, and LLM-assisted scoring
wildfire-mcp-server — MCP server for AI-assistant integration

items.title: Shahnameh Analyst — An AI Expert on Ferdowsi's Shahnameh
items.body:
Shahnameh Analyst — An AI Expert on Ferdowsi's Shahnameh
[author removed]
Abstract
Ask any general-purpose AI about a specific passage, character, or event in Ferdowsi's Shahnameh and you will likely get a vague or inaccurate answer. These models were trained on whatever fragments of the text happened to appear on the internet — they do not have access to every word of the book, nor do they carry the scholarly interpretations needed to understand it deeply.
Shahnameh Analyst solves this by giving an AI agent direct access to the complete, verified text of the Shahnameh along with curated expert interpretations. The result is a tool that can answer detailed questions about any verse, story, character, or theme in the book — precisely and with references — something no existing LLM can do on its own.
The project currently works as an AI agent (MCP server), but can evolve into a fine-tuned LLM specialized in Shahnameh and Persian literary heritage.
Two repositories are already in place and can quickly become a working MVP:

shahnameh-mcp-server — The AI agent server that provides precise, source-backed answers about Shahnameh
shahnameh-dataset — The complete Shahnameh text and expert interpretations as structured data

Why It's Interesting

Shahnameh is the backbone of Iranian cultural memory. It is far more than a poem — it is a summary of Iran's ancient history woven with stories rooted in real events. For Iranians, knowing the Shahnameh is essential to understanding their own identity. Making it deeply accessible through AI serves an entire culture.
No existing AI can do this well. General-purpose LLMs give shallow or incorrect answers about Shahnameh because they lack the full text and scholarly context. This project fills that gap with a complete, expert-curated dataset — not random internet text.
It serves a wide audience. Shahnameh scholars (شاهنامه‌پژوهان), students, casual readers, content creators looking for accurate source material, and non-Iranians curious about Persian literature and Iran's history — all benefit from a reliable AI expert on this book.
It promotes Persian literature globally. An accessible, high-quality AI tool about Shahnameh can introduce this masterpiece to the world in a way that books alone cannot. It helps content creators produce well-researched material and lowers the barrier for anyone who wants to learn.
It can be used in education. Schools and universities can integrate it as a study aid, making the Shahnameh approachable for students who might otherwise find classical Persian challenging.

Approach
Phase 1 — Build the MVP (Now)

Finalize the MCP server with the complete Shahnameh text and existing expert interpretations
Enable precise verse-level search, character lookup, and story summaries
Deploy as an agent that can be used through AI assistants (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT via MCP)
Team needed: developers only

Phase 2 — Deepen the Knowledge

Collaborate with Persian literature scholars and Shahnameh experts to enrich the dataset with deeper interpretations, historical context, and cross-references
Add support for multiple scholarly commentaries and variant readings
Explore fine-tuning a specialized LLM on the curated Shahnameh corpus

Phase 3 — Expand and Promote

Build a public-facing web interface and mobile app for direct access
Collaborate with marketing and outreach people to promote the tool to content creators, educators, and the global audience
Seek partnerships with universities, cultural institutions, and Persian studies programs
Extend to other major works of Persian literature (Hafez, Rumi, Nizami)

Help Needed

Developers — to build and refine the MVP (MCP server, dataset tooling, API)
Persian Literature & Shahnameh Experts — to validate and enrich the dataset with scholarly interpretations (Phase 2)
Marketing & Outreach — to promote the tool to content creators, educators, and the global Persian-studies community (Phase 3)
Partnership Builders — to connect with universities, cultural organizations, and media

Supporting Material

Live repositories:

shahnameh-mcp-server — AI agent server for precise Shahnameh Q&A
shahnameh-dataset — Complete Shahnameh text and expert interpretations as structured data


Key differentiator: Unlike general LLMs, this system has access to every word of the Shahnameh and expert-curated interpretations — enabling precise, verifiable answers
Future direction: From AI agent to fine-tuned LLM specialized in Persian literary heritage

items.title: The Citizen-Shareholder: A Financial Architecture for Oil & Gas Capital Management of Iran
items.body:
All numbers and ratios are approximate and require precise calculations.
The Core Idea:
The 30/70 Stakeholder Model.
Natural resources (Oil, Gas, Minerals) are transformed from "Government Assets" into "Citizen-Equity." The State ceases to be the owner-operator. Instead, 70% of operations are privatized to companies, while 30% of net profits are captured as a People’s Wealth Dividend owned directly by the people through a multi-tiered fund system.
That 70% can be divided among multiple smaller firms or consortia to prevent a single mega-monopoly. These companies acquire their shares through highly transparent public auctions or via the Stock Market, where all bidding data and financial qualifications are accessible to the general public in real-time.
Why? (The Problem)
•	The Rentier Trap: When the government owns the oil, it doesn't need the people's taxes, leading to a "Master-Subject" relationship rather than "State-Citizen."
•	Dutch Disease: Influx of petrodollars into local budgets causes inflation and kills non-oil industries (e.g., manufacturing).
•	The Corruption Black Box: State-run oil companies lack transparency, becoming the primary source of political patronage and embezzlement.
How? (The Structural Blueprint)
•	The Private Sector (70%): Ownership and management are held by a diverse pool of private entities. This 70% can be fragmented into multiple smaller firms to prevent a single mega-monopoly. Entry is strictly through public auctions or the stock market, with all bidding data publicly available.
•	The Provincial Wealth Fund (15%): Owned by citizens of the resource-bearing province (e.g., Khuzestan, Bushehr). Constraint: Must be invested in projects outside its own province (in other Iranian states to create national unity and prevent inflation).
•	The National Wealth Fund (15%): Owned by all Iranians equally. Constraint: Must be invested in global markets (stocks/tech/ETFs, etc.) to shield the economy from local shocks.
•	The Governance Layer (25% Corporate Tax): 10% for Provincial Infrastructure, schools, and local police. And 15% for national defense and diplomacy.
Why This Works? (The Mechanism)
•	Decoupling the Budget: The government lives only on the 25% tax. If the private sector fails, the government starves. This forces the state to be pro-business and pro-rule-of-law.
•	Anti-Inflation Shield: By forcing investments outside the local area (inter-state or International), you prevent "hot money" from overheating the local economy and causing price spikes.
•	Global Accountability: All funds are subject to mandatory auditing by reputable international firms to ensure they meet global standards of honesty.
•	Radical Transparency: Every citizen has a mobile dashboard to monitor exactly where, how much, and why funds are being invested in real-time.
•	Transparency by Design: Since 30% of profits go to funds audited by the Independent Legal Meritocracy (Judiciary), every barrel of oil must be accounted for on a public, digital ledger.
•	Anti-Monopoly Protocols: Stringent constitutional "Anti-Trust" laws prevent the 70% private ownership from consolidating into a new class of oligarchs.
Impact? (The Socio-Political Result)
•	Economic Interdependence: Provinces become "shareholders" in each other, making secession economically suicidal. A resource-rich province will not secede because its wealth is invested in the neighboring states' industries.
•	The Birthright Dividend: Every child receives a "Birthright Share." While the principal is protected, the profits are fully liquid, allowing citizens to trade, spend, or save their wealth freely. The citizen is no longer a beggar of the state but a Shareholder of the Nation.
•	Freedom of the Press: Investigative journalists are constitutionally protected to act as the final watchdog over auctions and fund management.
•	The Death of the Dictator’s Wallet: No central leader can "turn off the tap" or use oil money to buy loyalty, as the money never enters the central executive’s bank account.
The Approach (Implementation Strategy)
•	Legal Meritocracy: Fund managers are appointed by the Provincial Council and vetted by the Judiciary, ensuring expert management over political loyalty.
•	Digital Democracy: Use the dividend app as a tool for mass public monitoring, making every citizen a guardian of the nation’s wealth.
•	Regional Pacification: By giving the 10% local tax and 15% local profit to provinces, regions gain financial autonomy without threatening the national integrity.
•	Anti-Monopoly Protocols: Stringent "Anti-Trust" laws are embedded in the Constitution to ensure the 70% private ownership does not consolidate into a new class of oligarchs.

کویر شهداد یکی از منحصربه فردترین نقاط ایران است به طوری که گرمترین نقطه کره زمین توسط ناسا در این مکان ثبت شده از طرفی این کویر وسیع مناسب ترین مکان برای ستاره نگری است. راه اندازی بزرگترین مرکز پژوهش های فضایی و اقلیم شناسی در این منطقه علاوه بر ایجاد فرصت های شغلی و آبادانی در جنوب شرق کشور، زمینه همکاری های تناتنگ با ESA و  NASA را هم فراهم می کند. مزیت های راه اندازی بزرگترین مرکز فضاشناسی در کویر شهداد:

اقلیم خشک و پایدار: افزایش دقت تست ها
اختلاف دمای شدید شب و روز و دمای بسیار بالا در تابستان: شبیه سازی در اقلیم های سخت
مرکز زدایی لجستیکی از پایتخت
ایجاد فرصت های شغلی علمی غیر وابسته به مشتقات نفت و گاز در جنوب شرق
فاصله کافی از مراکز شهری برای پرتاب های آزمایشی
آسمان پاک با کمترین آلودگی نوری

items.body:
معماری سنتی ایرانی از نظر تنوع، زیبایی، قدمت و هم خوانی با اقلیم ایران منحصر به فرد است. پژوهش ها نشان داده اند که خانه های با سقف گنبدی و وجود طاق و قوس علاوه بر خنک نگه داشتن هوا، مقاومت بنا را در برابر زلزله بالا میبرد. استفاده مجدد از کاشی کاری، آینده کاری، پنجره های رنگی، ایوان، حیاط مرکزی و حوض که همگی جز عناصر معماری ایرانی هستند در ساخت و سازهای آینده علاوه بر پیوند عمیق با ریشه های فرهنگی مان، تاثیر بسزایی در زیبایی بصری و جذب توریسم خواهد داشت.
از طرفی با توجه به زلزله خیز بودن بسیاری از مناطق ایران، پیشنهاد می شود که با آموزش مهندسان ایرانی، از پیشرفتهای چشمگیر ژاپن در ساخت بناهای بسیار مقاوم به زلزله استفاده شود.

items.title: The Role of Learning Management Systems in Rebuilding Education in Iran
items.body:
A Learning Management System (LMS) provides a centralized digital platform for delivering, managing, and tracking educational content, communication, and assessment. As a flexible, scalable, and user friendly infrastructure, an LMS enables institutions to support both in person and remote learning, streamline administrative processes, and ensure consistent access to high quality educational resources. In Iran,  modern LMS platforms can play a transformative role in rebuilding and democratizing the education system. They decrease unequal access to learning materials, outdated pedagogical methods, and regional disparities in educational quality. A LMS enables transparent evaluation, open access to curriculum, and data driven decision making, which supports institutional reform. Moreover, it empowers students through self paced study and online accessibility to course materials.
A LMS is an appealing learning platform because it gives students a complete and transparent view of their course from the very beginning. The entire structure, modules, schedule, assignments and deadlines, is organized in one place, allowing students to understand the flow of the course and plan their work effectively. Through LMS platforms, students can submit homework, receive feedback, and communicate easily with instructors. It also provides built in tools for quizzes and tests, helping students evaluate their knowledge and track their understanding throughout the semester.
A LMS platform is particularly interesting because it is designed around the latest findings in pedagogical research, emphasizing transparency of intended learning outcomes, active learning, and student-centered learning. In a country like Iran, where the education system has long been centralized and restrictive, adopting a LMS platform would be especially important.
Building an LMS platform in a country like Iran requires a phased and strategic approach that begins with assessing national infrastructure, digital access, and institutional readiness. The new government defines its educational vision and pedagogical strategy to ensure the system aligns with modern learning principles. A realistic timeline would include a pilot phase in selected regions, followed by a gradual nationwide rollout and continuous teacher training to guarantee effective adoption and long‑term success.
At the core, the project needs software engineers, system architects, and cybersecurity specialists to build, customize, and maintain a reliable digital infrastructure. Equally important are instructional designers, curriculum experts, and pedagogical researchers who can align the platform with modern learning principles and adapt content to local needs. In addition, partnerships with educational centres, telecom providers and private sectors are essential.
Zahra Motamedi
Armin Iravani

items.title: Zero-Hallucination Bilingual RAG Q&A Tool for Iran Prosperity Project Emergency Phase Documents
items.body:
[author removed]
Data Scientist & Applied ML/AI Engineer at Leiden University; independent open-source developer creating practical AI tools. Built this zero-hallucination bilingual RAG Q&A application over a single weekend as a solo project. Previously shared thoughts on AI for accessible policy analysis in a LinkedIn post (link: https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7437240210125598724/) Open to collaboration, feature contributions, handover for hosting, or joint development with interested teams/organizations. Contact: GitHub issues/DM, or via LinkedIn.
Abstract
A 100% local, offline-capable, bilingual (English ↔ فارسی) Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) application that answers questions about the Iran Prosperity Project’s Emergency Phase policy booklet (~370 pages / 178-page English PDF + Persian version) using only direct quotes from the source documents, with mandatory [Page X] citations per sentence. Designed to eliminate hallucinations completely via strict retrieval thresholds, citation verification, extractive-only LLM prompting, and no generation if no good matches. Runs via Docker Compose + Ollama (Qwen 2.5) on any laptop/server — ideal for researchers, journalists, policymakers, or citizens needing verifiable, source-grounded insights during Iran's transitional phase.
Why It’s Interesting
The Emergency Phase booklet is a concrete, detailed blueprint for the first 180 days post-transition (governance, economy, security, rights, etc.), published by NUFDI / Iran Prosperity Project. Most people won't read 370+ pages — this tool makes the content instantly queryable and trustworthy. It's timely for the current short-term/transitional needs in Iran: accurate info without internet dependency or risk of AI fabrication. Full Persian RTL support + hybrid search makes it usable inside Iran. Built over one weekend as an open-source starting point for the community.
Approach
Ingest PDFs (pdfplumber with RTL fix) → multilingual-e5-large embeddings + BM25 hybrid retrieval → cross-encoder reranking.
Local LLM (Ollama + Qwen 2.5 7B/14B) forced extractive-only.
Multiple hallucination blocks: cosine ≥0.38, short-circuit on poor retrieval, citation checker post-answer.
Nice web UI (FastAPI + HTML/JS) at localhost:7860.
One-command setup via Docker Compose (downloads model on first run).
Includes eval suite for faithfulness/relevance testing.
Status: Working MVP, public repo, MIT license — ready for anyone to fork, extend (add more docs, API, voice, etc.), or host publicly.
Help Needed
Short-term hosting/deployment: Anyone with server access (VPS, cloud credits, institutional hosting) who can deploy a public instance (e.g., via Render, Railway, Hugging Face Spaces, or a simple EC2/DigitalOcean droplet) so non-technical users can try it online without installing anything. Happy to assist with setup/handover.
Persian speakers to run Farsi test queries and report issues/improvements.

Connections to NUFDI, diaspora tech groups, journalists, or transition-planning orgs who might integrate/extend this or provide more policy docs.
General feedback, stars/forks, real-world usage stories.
